How do you design memory technology that delivers high performance while keeping power consumption and silicon area to a minimum? At Xenergic, it starts with a deep understanding of analog circuits, advanced semiconductor technology and the ability to turn complex design challenges into working solutions. We are now looking for an Analog Design Engineer to join our team in Lund and contribute to the development of our next generation of on-chip memory IP.
YOU WILL
 Xenergic is a Lund-based semiconductor company developing high-speed, low-power on-chip memory IP for advanced chip technologies. Our engineering teams work with technology that ranges from transistor-level circuit design to physical implementation, verification and integration into customers' products.  As an Analog Design Engineer, you will join a specialised engineering team developing and optimising the analog circuits behind Xenergic's memory technology. You will contribute to new designs and improvements to existing solutions, using your understanding of the broader memory architecture to guide design decisions.  Your main responsibilities will be to:

Design and optimise analog circuits and custom IC blocks for advanced SRAM and memory IP.

Work with transistor-level and schematic design, including circuit simulation and verification across different operating conditions.

Analyse circuit behaviour and optimise designs for power consumption, performance, silicon area and reliability.

Contribute to physical layout, design verification and analysis of layout-related effects, including parasitics and EMIR.

Support the development and adaptation of memory IP across different semiconductor process technologies.

Collaborate with colleagues across analog, digital, layout and verification to solve technical challenges and support integration into customer designs.

You will join an analog team of six engineers with different technical backgrounds and experience. The team holds regular technical discussions to share challenges, design decisions and possible improvements. Much of the work requires independent problem-solving, alongside close collaboration to develop the technology. Depending on the project, you may also participate in technical discussions with customers.
The position is full-time and based on-site at Xenergic's office in Lund.
YOU ARE
You hold an M.Sc. in Electronics Engineering, Microelectronics or a related field, or have gained equivalent expertise through relevant industry experience. You have at least three years of professional experience in analog IC design, including transistor-level design, schematic development and simulation.
You have a good understanding of CMOS circuit design and are comfortable analyzing simulation results and optimizing circuits for power, performance and area. You have experience with Cadence Virtuoso, Spectre or comparable EDA tools, along with an understanding of how physical layout and parasitic effects influence circuit performance.
Experience in SRAM or memory design is an advantage but not required. Knowledge of advanced technology nodes, FinFET, DRC/LVS, EMIR-aware design, silicon measurements or scripting languages such as Python, shell or SKILL would also be an advantage.
 As a person, you are curious, analytical and enjoy understanding how things work, from individual circuits to broader architecture. You take ownership of your work, enjoy solving problems independently and value collaboration with colleagues. You are comfortable working in a smaller organization where learning, flexibility and sharing knowledge are part of everyday work. Fluency in English is required.
At Xenergic, you will work alongside experienced engineers in a highly specialized environment where your ideas and technical contributions can make a real difference. You will have the opportunity to influence the development of advanced memory technology and see your work become part of products used by customers around the world
WANT TO KNOW MORE? 
In this recruitment, Xenergic is collaborating with Nexer Recruit. Applications are reviewed continuously, so please submit your application as soon as possible. For questions about the role or the recruitment process, please contact recruitment consultant Johanna Värmfors at johanna.varmfors@nexergroup.com or +46 730 821 230, or Artan Bitiqi at artan.bitiqi@nexergroup.com or +46 723 61 28 44.
We look forward to hearing from you.
ABOUT XENERGIC
Xenergic is a Swedish deep-tech semiconductor technology company based in Lund, developing high-speed and low-power on-chip memory IP for advanced semiconductor applications. Its technology addresses important challenges in modern chip design, where performance, power consumption and silicon area are becoming increasingly important. Xenergic's solutions are relevant for applications ranging from IoT and mobile devices to networking, high-performance computing and AI.

TL;DR — You'll make sure no one at Lovable spends time on anything AI can do. We're defining how AI-native companies operate internally, across Product, GTM, and G&A. You'll own the systems that let a 300-person team move like a 3,000-person company: workflow automations, internal AI tools, data enrichment pipelines. You'll use Lovable itself to build much of this. This role is part of Project Automate Lovable, working closely with our AI Operations & Automation function and FBOS team.
Why Lovable?
Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.
We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.
Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.
What we’re looking for
Shipped production automations at a company: You've built workflow systems at scale that ran without you. Actual business-critical automations used by teams.
Engineering brain, modern toolkit: You understand how systems actually work (APIs, databases, architecture) and can review code confidently. You move fast by choosing the right tool for the job: AI agents (Cursor, Claude Code etc) when they're faster, no-code (Lovable itself, n8n, Clay, etc.) when it fits, raw code when it's needed.
Data is part of your building material: You can turn fragmented data across tools, databases, and external sources into reliable, usable systems. You’re comfortable designing data models, writing complex SQL, building enrichment and transformation pipelines, and creating the feedback loops that keep data trustworthy over time.
AI tool obsessed: You're always testing the latest models, apps, and workflows before anyone else. You've deployed internal AI tools (Claude/ChatGPT with custom contexts, AI agents, MCPs, etc.) at a company and you're constantly experimenting with new ones.
Can't unsee inefficiency: You see the whole company as one machine. Once you spot a broken process, you can't leave it alone.
High agency: You don't wait for permission. You find the bottleneck, build the fix, and ship it.

What you’ll do
Own internal AI systems that make Lovable run faster than it should.
Define how AI-native companies operate: Help build the playbook. What we learn here scales to every company using Lovable.
Build internal tools and workflows: Using Lovable, AI agents, no-code, raw code—whatever gets the job done fastest. Lovable on Lovable first, always.
Turn company data into operational leverage: Connect and enrich data across our stack, then put it directly to work, powering automations, internal tools, AI agents, decision-making, and proactive workflows across Finance, Business Operations, Legal, etc.
Deploy AI agent armies: Claude/ChatGPT with MCPs configured so every teammate has AI working for them, not the other way around.
Squeeze value from our stack: Make the AI features in Slack, Linear, Notion, Ashby, etc. actually deliver.
Level up the team: Turn everyone at Lovable into AI power users. Document what works. Scale it.
Own it end-to-end: You build it, you maintain it, you improve it.

About your application
Please submit your application in English. It’s our company language, so you’ll be speaking lots of it if you join.
We treat all candidates equally - if you’re interested, please apply through our careers portal.

jobs.occupation: Finance Business Partner - Northern Europe to KUKA Nordic
jobs.description:
KUKA Nordic is looking for an experienced Finance Business Partner to support the Northern Europe organisation across the Nordics, Baltics, the UK and Ireland. This is a broad regional role where you will combine financial expertise with business partnering, working closely with senior stakeholders to strengthen financial performance, governance and business decision-making.  If you are motivated by combining financial expertise with commercial impact, KUKA Nordic offers the opportunity to make a real difference across Northern Europe.

ABOUT THE ROLE
As Finance Business Partner, you will play a key role in supporting KUKA's Northern Europe organisation across the Nordics, Baltics, the UK and Ireland. As a member of the Northern Europe leadership team, you will combine financial expertise with commercial insight to support business decisions, strengthen financial governance and drive business performance across the region.
While transactional accounting and statutory reporting are managed by KUKA's Shared Service Center in Hungary, you will have the regional financial responsibility and act as the key link between the business, the SSC and Group Finance. Initially, the role requires a hands-on approach to support the ongoing transition and establish effective ways of working across the region.
Your responsibilities include:

Acting as a trusted Finance Business Partner to the Northern Europe leadership team and Country Managers.

Supporting strategic and commercial decision-making through financial analysis, business cases and performance insights.

Leading budgeting, forecasting, performance management, and KPI follow-up across the region.

Driving financial governance and ensuring high-quality financial reporting in collaboration with the Shared Service Center.

Coordinating audits, statutory compliance, tax matters and external stakeholders across multiple countries.

Monitoring working capital, cash flow and overall financial performance while identifying opportunities to improve business results.

Driving continuous improvements to finance processes and strengthening collaboration across the regional finance organisation.

ABOUT YOU
You are an experienced finance professional who enjoys working close to the business and understands the value of combining financial expertise with commercial insight. You thrive in an international environment, build trusted relationships across functions and countries, and are comfortable operating independently.
We believe you have:

A university degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics or Business Administration.

Several years of experience in Finance, Business Partnering or Controlling within an international organisation.

Familiarity with Shared Service Center or outsourced finance environments is preferred.

A good understanding of IFRS and the ability to understand and work with financial reporting. Previous hands-on reporting experience is advantage, but not a requierment.

An understanding of statutory and tax-related matters is a plus, while specialist tax expertise is not required.

Experience working across multiple countries and legal entities.

Strong Excel skills and, preferably, experience with SAP.

Fluency in English. Swedish or another Nordic language is considered an advantage.

As a person, you are proactive, curious and comfortable taking initiative. You work independently, structure and prioritise your own work, and have the drive to move topics forward.
You are a clear and confident communicator who builds effective relationships with different stakeholders. You combine an analytical mindset with a practical approach and are comfortable asking questions, challenging when appropriate and contributing your perspective in business discussions.

CONTACT
Does this opportunity sound interesting and align with your experience and ambitions? If so, we warmly welcome you to submit your application. In this recruitment process KUKA NORDIC cooperates with Committo. For more information, contact Linda Samuelsson at linda.samuelsson@committo.se or +46 702 16 37 52. As interviews and selection are conducted on an ongoing basis, we kindly ask you to submit your application as soon as possible. We look forward to hearing from you!

WHY KUKA NORDIC
At KUKA, you will become part of one of the world's leading automation companies, working in an international environment where collaboration, continuous improvement and innovation are at the heart of the business. This role offers broad regional responsibility, close interaction with senior management and the opportunity to contribute to the continued development of the finance organisation across Northern Europe.

ABOUT KUKA NORDIC
KUKA is a global automation corporation with sales of around 4 billion euro and approximately 15,000 employees. The company is headquartered in Augsburg, Germany. As one of the world’s leading suppliers of intelligent automation solutions, KUKA offers customers everything they need from a single source: from robots and cells to fully automated systems and their networking in markets such as automotive, electronics, metal & plastic, consumer goods, e-commerce/retail and healthcare.

Are you an experienced Project Manager with a passion for supply chain excellence, product introductions and supplier collaboration? Join Ascom in Gothenburg and play an important role in ensuring that our products are introduced and manufactured with the right quality, capacity and efficiency.
The role
As our Project Manager within Supply Chain, you will manage global supply chain projects from initial scope and planning through execution, follow-up and handover to the maintenance phase.
You will coordinate activities between main project and across Supply Chain, Quality, Purchasing, Logistics, R&D and other relevant functions, while working closely with our EMS and ODM suppliers. A key part of the role is ensuring that new products and manufacturing processes meet Ascom’s requirements regarding quality, capacity, cost, flexibility and lead time. The position is based at our office in Gothenburg and includes international collaboration and frequent travel to supplier sites.

Your responsibilities

Plan, lead and follow up supply chain projects, including scope, timelines, deliverables, risks and reporting.

Ensure quality assurance and on-time delivery throughout the project lifecycle.

Coordinate product introductions and secure a smooth transition into ramp-up, mass production and the maintenance phase.

Ensure that products are manufactured and repaired according to Ascom’s requirements for quality, capacity and lead time.

Manage project progress with EMS and ODM suppliers, including cost, quality management plans, yield, capacity, efficiency and pre-series activities.

Confirm that manufacturing processes and deliveries are developed, validated and ready for implementation.

Build and maintain strong relationships with suppliers and internal stakeholders.

Coordinate activities across Supply Chain, Quality, Purchasing, Logistics, R&D, Marketing and other relevant functions.

Support the continuous improvement and standardization of supply chain project methods, processes and ways of working.

Contribute to a stable, secure and continuously improving global supply chain. 

What you bring

A master’s degree in mechanical engineering, electronic engineering or a related technical field.

Several years of experience within Supply Chain, Manufacturing and/or Quality Assurance.

Proven experience leading projects and cross-functional project teams.

Strong knowledge of project management methods, planning, risk management and stakeholder coordination.

Strong understanding of electronic manufacturing processes, production flow, test methods and industrialization.

Experience working with external manufacturing partners, preferably EMS or ODM suppliers.

Experience and strong knowledge in translating technical requirements into clear manufacturing, supplier and quality deliverables.

A good understanding of electronic manufacturing processes, including production, testing, logistics, purchasing and quality assurance.

Experience building and developing strong, long-term supplier relationships.

Knowledge of ERP systems and good proficiency in Microsoft 365.

An understanding of Lean Production principles and continuous improvement.

Excellent communication skills and professional fluency in English. 

Who you are
You are a structured, proactive and technically skilled Project Manager with a strong understanding of production processes, engineering drawings and technical specifications. You can quickly identify gaps, clarify requirements and drive practical solutions together with suppliers and internal teams. You communicate clearly, follow up systematically and balance technical detail with project progress.
You are comfortable in bringing people, processes and priorities together while navigating complex projects where requirements may evolve and where successful outcomes depend on collaboration across organisational and geographical boundaries.

You have strong technical skills, communicate clearly, build trust with suppliers and colleagues, and know how to influence decisions without relying on formal authority. You combine attention to detail with a strong understanding of the bigger picture and are motivated by improving quality, efficiency and ways of working.

Why join Ascom?
At Ascom, your work supports technology and communication solutions that help improve efficiency and decision-making in healthcare and other mission-critical environments. You will join an international organization where high quality, collaboration, innovation and continuous improvement are central to how we work.

In this role, you will have the opportunity to:

Work in a global and cross-functional environment.

Collaborate with experienced colleagues and international suppliers.

Influence how new products are introduced and manufactured.

Contribute directly to supply chain quality, stability and performance.

Develop your expertise through challenging projects and continuous learning. 

Ready to join us?
If you are ready to take ownership of complex supply chain projects and contribute to the successful introduction of Ascom’s products, we would be happy to hear from you. Apply today and help us shape a reliable, efficient and future-ready supply chain.

Ascom is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to creating an inclusive working environment where everyone is treated fairly and has the opportunity to succeed.

Single Cell Discoveries is seeking a Site Director to lead and oversee all operations at our Gothenburg laboratory, TATAA Biocenter! 
This is a senior leadership role for a hands-on operational leader who thrives on responsibility, solving complex challenges, and can make confident decisions in a fast-moving environment while maintaining the highest standards of regulatory compliance. You will be responsible for all operations at Tataa Biocenter: People management, facility management, and site-wide coordination. You will ensure the site runs smoothly, the infrastructure and processes needed for compliance are in place, and our staff have everything they need to deliver exceptional results for sponsors around the world. The role reports directly to the COO, will be board facing and includes a place in the global group management team.
Are you energized by accountability, motivated by helping teams succeed, and eager to play a key role in a growing, accredited CRO? We would like to hear from you!
Who Are We? 
TATAA Biocenter, part of the Single Cell Discoveries Group, is a specialized molecular analysis CRO supporting pharmaceutical and biotech sponsors worldwide. Our laboratory is GCLP-compliant and accredited under GLP and ISO 17025:2017, with deep expertise in qPCR, dPCR, RNA-seq/NGS, and biomarker analysis. We combine scientific excellence with a collaborative and entrepreneurial culture, helping sponsors accelerate innovations in precision medicine.
As Site Director, you will work closely with laboratory teams, quality assurance, IT, business development, vendors, external partners, and company leadership to ensure the smooth and efficient operation of the entire site. You will report directly to the group COO.
What Will You Do?
Lead and oversee operations of the Gothenburg site.
Serve as a key point of escalation for laboratory staff, operational challenges, and project execution issues.
Ensure laboratory infrastructure, equipment, and facilities are maintained and operate efficiently.
Coordinate and manage relationships with vendors, service providers, contractors, engineers, and facility partners.
Support laboratory teams in prioritization, problem-solving, and operational decision-making.
Support capacity planning, resource allocation, and operational growth initiatives.
Provide strong site leadership, fostering a safe, compliant, and high-performing environment.
Represent site operations internally and externally, including during client, vendor, and regulatory interactions.
Have budget responsibility for all operations in our Gothenburg site.
Design strategies that fit the group’s goals and present progress to our COO and CEO, as well as our board.

Who Are We Looking For?
Essential
You hold a MSc or PhD in a relevant field, with significant industry experience (preferably within CRO or pharma bioanalytical setting).
You are an engaging people leader who motivates colleagues through energy, trust, and collaboration.
You have significant experience managing laboratory operations, preferably within a regulated environment.
You have experience working within regulated laboratory environments, including GxP frameworks (e.g., GLP, GCLP) and/or accredited quality systems such as ISO 17025. 
You are comfortable taking ownership and making decisions, including under time pressure.
You have a proven ability to coordinate multiple stakeholders and priorities simultaneously. 
You are a natural problem-solver who enjoys helping others overcome operational challenges.
You have experience working with external vendors, contractors, facility providers, and technical service partners. 
You possess excellent organizational and communication skills in English, both written and oral.

Preferred 
Experience acting as Test Site Manager, Deputy Test Site Manager, or in a similar regulated laboratory leadership role. 
Experience supporting inspections, audits, and accreditation activities.
Experience in a CRO, biotech, pharmaceutical, or life sciences environment
Experience presenting operational matters to senior leadership, company owners, or a board of directors. 

Who You Are 
You enjoy responsibility and proactivity.
You like making things happen.
You are approachable, and people naturally come to you with questions and challenges. 
You can switch effortlessly between discussions with scientists, engineers, vendors, and leadership teams. 
You bring energy, pragmatism, and common sense. 
You are decisive, confident, and action oriented. 
 Quality and accountability come naturally to you. 

Why Join TATAA?
A highly visible leadership role with significant influence on the future of the organization.
Ownership of laboratory operations within a growing and internationally recognized CRO.
The opportunity to work with talented scientists in a collaborative and entrepreneurial environment.
A role where your decisions directly impact employees, sponsors, and business success.
The chance to help shape the future of precision medicine and advanced molecular analysis.

Join us in accelerating innovations in precision medicine. 
Need more info? For questions about this opening or the recruitment process, please contact us at jobs@tataa.com.
Visit us at https://tataa.com/.

jobs.occupation: Executive Chef till Sheraton Stockholm Hotel
jobs.description:
A breakfast that starts the day right, a conference lunch that gets people talking, and a banquet that becomes part of the memory.
 
At Sheraton Stockholm, food is part of how we bring people together. With 463 rooms and 14 meeting rooms in the heart of the city, we welcome guests from around the world for stays, meetings and celebrations. As our hotel enters its next chapter, we’re looking for an Executive Chef to shape the culinary experience across breakfast, meetings, events and banqueting.
 
This is a role for someone who enjoys the scale and energy of a large international hotel. Someone who brings creativity to the menu, confidence to the operation and care to the way they lead. 
 
Join us and set the flavour of Sheraton Stockholm.
 
Big occasions and everyday details
You’ll take culinary ownership of these operations, setting the direction for the food and leading the kitchen organisation behind it. From the breakfast buffet to a working lunch or a large evening event, you’ll make sure every offering has a clear identity and delivers on taste, presentation and service.
 
You know that cooking at scale takes imagination and precision. You’ll develop seasonal menus and food experiences that suit different occasions, guest needs and budgets, while keeping execution consistent. Working closely with F&B and Events, you’ll turn each brief into an experience that works for the guest, the kitchen and the business.
 
You’ll also keep the operation moving forward: refining our breakfast offering, strengthening our meeting and event menus, and finding fresh ways to make hotel dining feel generous, relevant and memorable.
 
Lead the people and own the performance
Great food starts with a team that knows where it’s going. You’ll lead, coach and develop the kitchen leadership team and wider culinary organisation, building a culture of pride, collaboration and accountability. Clear expectations, constructive feedback and opportunities to grow will be part of everyday life in your kitchen.
 
You’ll take an active role in recruitment and talent development, building the skills and confidence needed to deliver across a demanding operation. You plan ahead, stay present during service and create structure that helps people perform at their best.
 
Commercial ownership comes with the role. You’ll manage food cost, recipe costing, purchasing, inventories and waste, translating financial and operational insights into practical improvements. You’ll balance staffing and productivity with a sustainable working environment, develop strong supplier relationships and maintain high standards of food safety, hygiene and compliance with Marriott requirements.
 
You’ll work closely with F&B, Events, Operations, Finance and the wider hotel leadership team, bringing a clear culinary perspective to shared decisions.
 
Bring your experience and your appetite for what’s next
You’re an experienced culinary leader with a strong background in upscale or luxury hotels, ideally as an Executive Chef, Executive Sous Chef or in a comparable senior role. You understand high-volume breakfast, meetings and banqueting, and have a track record of delivering quality across several services and events at once.
 
You’re confident developing menus and equally comfortable discussing food cost, staffing and operational performance. You spot opportunities, make thoughtful decisions and follow through. Your leadership is grounded and approachable, with high standards and a genuine investment in the people around you.
 
International experience is highly valued. We welcome the perspective and ideas it brings, alongside curiosity about our guests and the market we operate in. You communicate fluently in English, and Swedish or experience from the Nordic market is an advantage. You must have the right to work in Sweden.
 
Make your mark on an iconic Stockholm hotel
Sheraton Stockholm has been a meeting place since 1971. Now, with a major hotel transformation and fresh momentum, there’s an opportunity to build on that heritage and shape what comes next.
 
You’ll have room to influence the food, strengthen the operation and develop a team that takes pride in every service, from the first breakfast guest to the final course of the evening.
 
Are you ready to bring your ideas to the table?
We’d love to hear from you. Send us your application and tell us what you would bring to Sheraton Stockholm.

Volumental is a FitTech™ company used by footwear brands and retailers, matching people with shoes that truly fit through 3D scanning and machine learning.
Our vision is "a world without sizes, where every body fits." We work with brands like New Balance, Red Wing, Fleet Feet, and Vivobarefoot across 3,000+ stores in 60 countries, with 60M+ foot scans collected, one of the world's largest datasets of its kind.
We are 20+ nationalities based mostly in Stockholm, with colleagues across Europe, the US, and Asia. People & Culture is a team of two (Head of People & Culture + Office Coordinator), and you’ll be our third. We’re small, but our work has real business impact. We strengthen leadership, keep our processes and policies evolving with the business, and foster an environment where people do their best work.
 Where you fit in
The foundations are in place. Much of our admin is outsourced, automated, or increasingly handled by AI agents. Managers own day-to-day processes, supported by toolkits and coaching.
We’re now looking for a Senior People Partner to shape what comes next. You’ll look at how we work and make it better: rethinking tooling, building new agents and automations while keeping the human touch, anticipating what the business will need next, and finding new ways for People & Culture to create impact.
This role suits a builder with good judgment. You’ll enjoy making recurring work smaller: automating what should be automated, deleting what shouldn’t exist, and rebuilding what people work around. You’ll also build trust quickly to collaboratively solve problems as we grow.
 What you’ll do

Partner with managers, using data, business understanding, and trusted relationships, to help them build engaged, high-performing teams.

Rethink recurring people work such as onboarding, probation, and development talks. Spot automation opportunities, and prototype solutions quickly.

Own and improve our people tooling (HiBob, Teamtailor, and our agents). Extract insights across People processes and use them to improve outcomes.

Run our company-wide cycles, such as salary reviews and engagement surveys, using our Manager Academy forum to prepare managers so each cycle runs smoothly.

Contribute team-level insights to workforce planning, organization decisions, engagement priorities and compensation decisions.

Balance employee experience, operational efficiency, and compliance in the everyday work that keeps everything running. 

What you'll need

6+ years of hands-on HR experience across the employee lifecycle, or deep expertise in at least three core areas of it (e.g., performance, compensation, onboarding, employee relations).

Experience implementing or redesigning company-wide performance, compensation, distributed workforce, or manager-enablement processes.

Experience adding features to or integrating an HRIS (HiBob or comparable).

Working fluency with AI tools and agents - you leverage AI tools in your day-to-day work (e.g., drafting, analysis, research) and know when to trust the output and when to check it.

A broad understanding of employment law.

Fluent English. 

How you work

You are pragmatic, structured, and enjoy building and iterating systems-level solutions for continuous improvement.

You get to the root of complex situations and make difficult people moments feel clear instead of chaotic.

You turn recurring questions and team-level signals into useful insights for managers.

You work well on your own and with others, and you can influence at every level.

You solve problems in the open, asking good questions, sharing your knowledge, and shipping first iterations sooner rather than presenting polished answers later.

You see things through, spotting what needs doing without being asked, and making it happen all the way to done.

Bonus - Not required, but nice to have

Experience at a tech scaleup, especially an engineering-heavy one.

Experience building automations or AI agents, using n8n, Zapier, Apps Script, MCP servers, or similar.

Familiarity with Swedish labor legislation.

Familiarity with remote work setups.

What we offer

Flexible work policy (at least 3 days from the office)

An AI-forward team that gives you the tools to work smarter

Personal learning budget and access to coaching

Occupational pension at ITP1 level

Flexible Public Holidays Policy

Options Program

Parental pay top-up

Wellness allowance

This is a full-time position based at our Stockholm headquarters, reporting to our Head of People & Culture. We welcome applicants from all background! If this role excites you but you don’t meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply - we’d love to hear from you.

About Univrses
Univrses is a Stockholm-based 3D Computer Vision and AI company. We provide the perception and spatial awareness necessary for an increasingly autonomous world. While our roots are in the automotive sector, we have pioneered a new category: Infrastructure Intelligence. Our 3DAI™ system transforms ordinary vehicles into sophisticated mobile sensors, providing road authorities across Europe (Sweden, UK, Italy, and beyond) with real-time, actionable insights. We are shifting city management from reactive repairs to proactive, data-driven maintenance—saving costs, reducing CO2 emissions, and improving public safety.
The Role
In your new developer role, you will take part in building the 3DAI™ platform. It is a scalable answer to the growing demand for data about the urban environment and part of our efforts in smart city development. You will play an important role in designing, building and scaling the platform. 3DAI™ is still a young product and you will have a lot to contribute and freedom to shape the project.

You will be responsible for growing our platform for storing, processing and visualizing data.

You will use your experience to design efficient solutions for our backend and frontend systems.

You will have the opportunity to create innovative technologies that will change people's lives and transform the world into a better place

Who you are
You have at least 3+ years of experience in Fullstack software development using Node.js and Typescript on the backend, and React (Vite SPA) on the frontend.

You are experienced with AWS cloud platform development.

You have excellent general understanding of REST APIs and GraphQL.

You are comfortable taking high-level front-end designs and turning that into readable, maintainable, best-practice React code.

You can build web-services from high level specifications, including figuring out database schemas, security considerations, logging and monitoring, and how best to scale out deployments to handle lots of users and data.

You have an enthusiasm to tackle large-scale data challenges, with prior experience on high-performance analytic databases as a bonus.

You like working in a team and sharing your knowledge. You are open to giving advice and listening to feedback.

You are passionate about writing high-quality code and care for ensuring code validity by writing unit and integration tests.

You keep up-to-date with best practices and new technologies.

You have an aspiration to see your ideas move into production.

Bonus points
You have experience working with any of these systems or technologies:

Serverless computing (e.g. AWS Lambdas)

Familiar to infrastructure as code technologies such as Docker, AWS Cloudformation/CDK

Geo spatial tools and databases such as PostGIS

MUI (Material-UI) based front-end components

E2E testing frameworks like Playwright

What’s in it for You?
We provide the environment and the tools for you to do the best work of your career.

Responsibility: Become a true stakeholder in a small team where your work actually matters.

Professional Evolution: You will be working on exciting projects involving game-changing technology with an opportunity to improve the world through autonomy and intelligence

The "Work-Life" Blend: Enjoy flexible work hours and a culture that values output over "desk time".

Upsides: A secure Pension Plan and Wellness activities for up to 5 000 SEK per year paid by the company.

The Univrses Culture:

Monday Momentum: Kick off the week with team breakfast.

Thursday Knowledge: Weekly Lunch & Learns where internal or external speakers present interesting topics, while the company pays for and caters the lunch to keep your technical and commercial skills sharp.

Friday Wind-down: Celebrate the week’s wins with our Friday After Work sessions (free beer from our well-curated beer fridge!)

The Workspace: A bright, collaborative office in Stockholm equipped with the essentials (yes, including the mandatory startup ping-pong table).

Are You Our Next Full Stack Engineer?
If you are a driven, creative strategist ready to shape the future of autonomous systems, we want to hear from you.
To apply, please include the following:

Your CV

A link to your LinkedIn profile

A brief introduction (tell us about a time you turned a challenging customer situation into a success).

Note: All application materials must be in English.

The opportunity
What if your next role puts you at the center of multi-million-dollar projects transforming the energy system? As a Senior Tender Manager, you will shape and execute bid strategies for large, complex HVDC pursuits, coordinating multidisciplinary teams and shaping solutions that bring together capabilities from across the Hitachi Energy portfolio. From defining the bid strategy to presenting a compelling technical and commercial offering to the customer, you will play a central role in winning the projects that will shape the future power grid.
“At Bid & Proposals, we lead the tendering of large-scale HVDC greenfield projects worldwide. My team focuses on the Northern European (NEU) market and is based in Sweden and the UK. Last year alone, our department secured 5 HVDC projects across the NEU region, giving our team a direct role in shaping Hitachi Energy’s business pipeline. We play a key role in driving business growth, supporting net-zero targets, and helping secure Europe’s energy supply..” – Louise Hellman, Hiring Manager.
Your base will be in Ludvika or Västerås, Sweden, and you will be part of the HVDC product group within Hitachi Energy. HVDC technology has been on the market for the past 60 years and is used to transmit power over long distances with minimal losses, using overhead lines, underground and submarine cable systems.
Come as you are and be ready to learn. Bring your passion, your energy, and join a team that appreciates a simple truth: Diversity + Collaboration = Innovation.
How you´ll make an impact
You will be leading a Bid & Proposal team of technical, commercial, legal, tax and insurance experts from early pursuit stage to contract signing and execution handover.
Interpret customer requirements and translate them into a competitive end-to-end solution based on Hitachi Energy’s portfolio.
You will shape and drive the overall tender strategy, aligning technical solutions, commercial positioning, pricing, risk and customer priorities.
Enjoy working on complex tenders from both technical and commercial perspectives and thrive in a high-performing international environment.
You will lead customer interactions, clarifications and commercial negotiations, building strong relationships throughout the tender process.
Demonstrate Hitachi Energy’s core values of safety and integrity by taking responsibility for your actions and supporting your colleagues and the business.

Your background
Experience in large-scale system sales and tendering, or in managing large projects.
Bachelor’s or Masters degree in Business, Technical, or a related field.

Xenergic is a Swedish semiconductor technology company based in Lund, developing high-speed, On-chip memory IP for advanced semiconductor applications.

Job Scope 
Why does the role exist? High level purpose of function. 
The Senior Manufacturing Engineer plays a key role in process equipment commissioning, production ramp-up, and full-scale manufacturing within a battery cell production facility. They ensure smooth start-up of production lines, optimize manufacturing processes, and lead continuous improvement initiatives to maximize process yield, equipment availability, and overall production performance. This role combines hands-on equipment commissioning experience, cross-functional collaboration, and technical expertise to deliver safe, efficient, and high-quality battery cell production. A Senior Manufacturing Engineer is responsible for all aspects of their process machine including technical functionality, how personnel interact with it, what maintenance activities are recommended and what crucial spares are required. 
Key Responsibilities 
Overall areas of responsibilities and activities 
Key responsibilities include (but are not limited to) 
Participate in HAZOP (Hazard & Operability Study) sessions and ensure compliance with process safety, operational safety, and environmental standards.  
Promote a culture of safety, quality, and operational excellence throughout production and commissioning activities.  
Lead process equipment commissioning, including cold and hot commissioning on-site during start-up or restart projects. (Project timeline dependent)  
Facilitate smooth transitions from commissioning to production ramp-up and full-scale manufacturing. (Project timeline dependent)  
Translate lessons learned into design and process improvements for future expansions.  
Monitor, analyze and improve production KPIs, including yield, availability, and performance. Identifying top losses, production bottlenecks, and performance gaps to drive corrective actions and continuous improvement initiatives.  
Lead root cause analysis (RCA) for equipment-related losses, minor stops, and process deviations.  
Define, release, and maintain manufacturing process standards and operator training programs.  
Train and mentor new engineers, operators and other support functions.  
Prepare, review, and approve documentation including (but not limited to WI, PFMEAs, commissioning checklists, project timelines, A3s).   
Provide technical feedback and guidance to suppliers to ensure equipment quality, compliance with specifications, and CE standards.  
Develop and issue DOEs (Design of Experiments) and schedule process and equipment trials onsite and at supplier sites (if required).  
Deliver a line capable of obtaining PPAP approval, following a structured quality gate model.   
Guide and mentor colleagues to industrial best practices, focusing on growth and development.  
Complete supplementary tasks as seen fit by management to effectively utilize time and resource for the benefit of the business.  
This role requires regular presence on the production floor. 

 Requirements 
Educational background and previous experience required for the role 
Qualifications and Experience 
Master's degree in mechanical, electrical, or chemical engineering.  
Minimum of 7 years of relevant work experience in production, equipment, or engineering-related roles.  
Proven track record of leading manufacturing process improvements and production optimization in a factory environment following recognised project management techniques.   
Experience in building and scaling production in a fast-growing environment, ideally within the battery, food, pharma, paper & pulp, semiconductor, electrochemical, or similar industries.  
Hands-on experience and interest in equipment commissioning, troubleshooting, and optimisation.  
Proficient in detailed root cause analysis, structured problem-solving methodologies and continuous improvement.  
Familiarity with quality assurance troubleshooting tools.  
Experience working to industry standards obtaining certification including ISO, IATF &VDA.  
Experience with statistical process control and process capability analysis. 
Experience working with preventive maintenance strategies and Total Productive Maintenance (TPM) concepts within a production environment. 
Experience in spare part prioritisation and stock optimisation, balancing equipment availability with cost efficiency. 

 Specific skills & Knowledge  
Strong knowledge of mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, and pneumatic systems.  
Knowledge of OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) metrics and their application in production environments.  
Knowledge of lean manufacturing principles and six sigma methodologies.  
Highly autonomous with a proactive mindset and work ethic.   
Strong technical curiosity, analytical mindset, and business-oriented problem-solving skills.  
Troubleshooting skills with diagnostic equipment.  
Ability to document technical problems concisely.  
Proficient in the use of a Computerised Maintenance Management System (CMMS) for work order management, equipment data, and maintenance reporting. Experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365 is advantageous. 
Experience in coaching, upskilling, and mentoring engineers or technicians, with a demonstrable commitment to developing the technical capability of others within a production environment. 
Excellent English skills, both written and oral, are essential. Basic Swedish and other language skills are a plus. You should have good communication skills and be able to work in close collaboration with colleagues from many different teams.  
Ability to work within varying environments including clean-rooms and dry-rooms, while wearing appropriate PPE.  
Comfortable operating in high-profile, international, and high-pressure environments.  
A genuine technical interest and passion about working within production is highly valued.

Make your mark. Grow with us. 
 
Your team 
Analytical Development – Protein Chemistry is part of Galderma's Injectables Development organization in Uppsala. The team provides analytical expertise that supports the development of innovative products and technologies, helping to strengthen and expand Galderma's portfolio.
You will join a collaborative and highly engaged team where knowledge sharing, scientific curiosity, and mutual support are valued. Together, we work in a dynamic environment where quality, innovation, and patient focus guide everything we do.
 
Your mission
As a Scientist within Analytical Development – Protein Chemistry, you will plan, perform, and interpret analytical studies supporting product and process development. You will contribute to solving complex analytical challenges related to proteins and biologics while ensuring that all activities are conducted in accordance with applicable quality standards and regulatory requirements.
Working closely with colleagues across Development, Quality, Regulatory Affairs, and other functions, you will play an important role in advancing development projects from early-stage investigations through method validation and implementation.
This role offers a broad range of scientific and technical challenges, providing opportunities to deepen your expertise while contributing to projects with real impact on Galderma's future portfolio.
 
Key responsibilities
· Develop, optimize, and validate analytical methods for proteins and related biological materials.
· Plan, execute, analyze, and document experimental work.
· Interpret analytical data and provide scientifically sound conclusions and recommendations.
· Author protocols, reports, SOPs, and other technical documentation.
· Provide analytical expertise and support within cross-functional development projects.
· Ensure that all activities are performed in accordance with GMP, internal procedures, and relevant regulatory requirements.
· Support project teams by identifying scientific solutions to analytical challenges.
· Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives within the laboratory and analytical development processes.
 
Your profile 
You are a curious and collaborative scientist who enjoys combining scientific expertise with practical problem-solving. You are motivated by understanding complex biological systems and translating analytical results into meaningful insights that support product development.
You thrive in an environment where teamwork, scientific discussion, and continuous learning are valued. At the same time, you take ownership of your work, approach challenges with a structured mindset, and maintain a strong focus on quality and scientific integrity.
You are comfortable working in project-based environments, communicating complex information clearly, and collaborating with colleagues from different disciplines and backgrounds.
 
What you'll bring
To be successful in this role, you bring:
· A university degree in Biochemistry, Molecular Biology, Biology, Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a related scientific discipline.
· Experience working within the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, or broader life sciences industry.
· Strong knowledge of analytical chemistry, biochemistry, protein characterization, or related scientific fields.
· Experience with analytical method development and validation.
· Experience working in regulated environments and familiarity with GMP and associated quality requirements.
· Experience interpreting regulatory guidelines, pharmacopeias, and scientific standards.
· Fluency in both English and Swedish, written and spoken.
 
Preferred qualifications

Immunology and anti-drug antibody (ADA) testing.
Protein therapeutics, biologics, or biosimilar development.
Advanced protein characterization techniques.
Analytical support in cross-functional development projects.
Statistical evaluation of analytical data.

 
Location and other
This position is based on site in Uppsala, Sweden. Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis, and the position may be filled before the application deadline. Please note that Galderma may conduct pre-employment background and security checks for certain positions. These checks are performed by an external provider and only with the candidate's consent.

You'll join a team of talented colleagues and play an important role in supporting the continued growth of our biologics and protein-based portfolio.

jobs.description:
Job Description

WHAT YOU’LL DO​
As a Sales Advisor at H&M, you’ll play a key role in creating an outstanding customer experience. You’ll welcome customers, guide them through your store, and support them in finding what they need while showcasing our products. Acting in line with our values, you’ll contribute to both your own success and the success of the company.
You will:
Share your fashion and product knowledge to help customers make informed choices.
Collaborate with your team to deliver exceptional service at every step of the customer journey.
Ensure the sales floor and back of house are well-stocked, organized, and inviting.
Support with opening and closing of the store.
Represent yourself and the brand positively during all customer interactions.

WHO YOU’LL WORK WITH​
Our stores are the heart of our company, where customers experience our brand firsthand. As part of the dynamic Store Team, every role—from Sales Advisors, Department Managers, Store Managers and Visual Merchandisers to Assistant Store Managers, Cash Office Responsible, and Delivery Responsible in larger stores—contributes to creating an inspiring and welcoming environment. You’ll also connect with the wider Area Team, collaborating across stores to share insights and drive success together. Alongside your team, you'll play a vital role in helping customers feel confident and express their individuality with the latest trends and timeless styles. By building meaningful connections with customers in our stores, we make fashion accessible and sustainable for all.
WHO YOU ARE​
We are looking for people with…​
Experience in customer service within fashion, retail, or similar fields.

And people who are…​
Passionate about fashion and delivering an exceptional in-store experience while promoting our products and driving sales.
Thriving in collaborative and dynamic environments.
Communicative, creative, curious to work with store technology, with a strong eagerness to learn and develop.
Flexible and action oriented.

WHO WE ARE​
H&M Group is a global company of strong fashion brands and ventures. Our goal is to prove that there is no compromise between exceptional design, affordable prices, and sustainable solutions. We want to liberate fashion for the many, and our customers are at the heart of every decision we make.​
​We are made up of thousands of passionate and talented colleagues united by our shared culture and values. Together, we want to use our power, our scale, and our knowledge to push the fashion industry towards a more inclusive and sustainable future. ​
WHY YOU’LL LOVE WORKING HERE ​
At H&M Group, we are proud to be a vibrant and welcoming company. We offer our employees attractive benefits with extensive development opportunities around the globe. ​
 All our employees receive a staff discount card, usable on all our H&M Group brands in stores and online. 
In addition to our staff discount, all our employees are included in our H&M Incentive Program – HIP. You can read more about our H&M Incentive Program here. 

JOIN US​
Our uniqueness comes from a combination of many things – our inclusive and collaborative culture, our strong values, and opportunities for growth. But most of all, it’s our people who make us who we are.​
This is a temporary on-demand position with no guaranteed hours. Work will be offered based on business needs with a start in December or by agreement. We are currently looking for people to our store located in Hässleholm and you should be available to work during store opening hours. Language skills in Swedish or English are required.
We have an ongoing selection, so the position may be filled before the application deadline, so send in your application today! The last application date is 25/11.
Take the next step in your career together with us. The journey starts here.​
 
* Store roles assessment: 
To manage the high volume of applications for the Sales Advisor role, we use an online assessment method for skills-based recruitment within some of our stores. You will need to complete it as part of the application and screening process. Your responses will be scored by an assessment tool that applies predefined criteria set by H&M Group. Please look out for an email in your inbox/junk email from MAKI. 
After completing the assessment, you’ll have the opportunity to share feedback and ask questions. If you experience any difficulties or prefer an alternative assessment method, please contact recruitment_support@hm.com. Choosing an alternative will not impact on your application. 
For more information on how we process your personal data, please see our Privacy Notice. 
** We are committed to a recruitment process that is fair, equitable, and based on competency. We therefore kindly ask you to not attach a cover letter in your application.

We are looking for a dedicated Imaging Engineer to strengthen our team! In this role you will further develop the imaging platform for our production systems but also support industrialization and R&D to turn new products and ideas into mass production. Does this sound interesting? Keep reading and welcome with your application!

Who is your future team?
You will join the Imaging team, a specialized group of four experienced engineers focused on developing the imaging parts needed within our production systems to produce Axis cameras with high image quality.

These production systems play a critical role in supporting high-volume manufacturing operations at our global facilities, where millions of products are produced and tested annually.

The Imaging team is part of a larger division of about 60+ engineers working with Production Engineering and Technology (PET), and together with our colleagues within SW, electronics and mechanical engineering we develop and maintain production systems globally.

What you'll do here as Imaging Engineer
As an Imaging Engineer, you'll contribute to the design, development and maintenance of imaging production tests that enable the testing of Axis products in our production systems. You will also be a part of our development projects where we use innovative imaging and optical solutions to design efficient and reliable production systems.
Typical tasks include handling topics related to optics, collimators and other imaging equipment needed to produce Axis' products.
You will also play an important role in designing, developing, and maintaining software frameworks used for verification and calibration of our production systems. This includes collaborating with cross-functional teams to ensure seamless production processes.
Key responsibilities include:
Designing and maintaining both SW and HW for the imaging tests framework to support production processes.
Developing and maintaining software frameworks to facilitate machine monitoring, verification, calibration and production testing using C# and Python
Providing technical support to R&D product development initiatives
Analyzing production data to drive system improvements and innovation
Contributing to strategic planning for future imaging test development

Our team leverages a range of technologies, including:
Hardware like different types of optics and collimators
Programming languages: C#, Python, C++
Tools: Jira, Confluence, QlikView, Visual Studio, GitHub Copilot
Version control systems: Git, SVN, Gerrit
Continuous integration platforms: TeamCity
Agile methodologies

Who are we looking for/Who are you?
We think you are a dedicated engineer with skills in imaging, optics and software development who is curious, responsible, organized and methodical. You enjoy problem solving and working with both hardware and software. Ability to communicate is important as the role requires collaboration with other teams and departments. The work includes a lot of freedom and independence, which requires that you are proactive and take initiative.
We'd love to hear that you have:
Experience within optics, collimators or other imaging equipment
A huge interest in software development and optics
Finding solutions to complex technical problems
Interest in the complexity of production and creating efficient production systems for our factories around the world
University degree preferably within computer science, engineering, physics, electrical engineering or equivalent
At least a couple of years of experience from roles in a development organization
Good communication skills in English and Swedish, both in speech and writing

The position is full time. Travelling is not required, but there will probably be possibilities to visit our factories around the world.

What Axis has to offer
We are a world leader in network video, where cutting-edge technology meets global impact. 
Here, you'll contribute to meaningful projects that shape the future of security and surveillance - developing solutions used worldwide.
As a fast-growing company, we offer exciting career opportunities. You'll grow professionally through continuous learning, supported by a collaborative team that values creativity, innovation, and work-life balance. 
Your well-being matters to us. We offer a range of benefits, including a company bonus, Friday cake, wellness allowance, health insurance - and even your own Axis bicycle.
To learn more about Axis, our innovative products, solutions, and vibrant company culture, explore:
Life at Axis blog

Innovation at Axis

Ready to Act?
Axis is a company realizing the benefits of a diverse workforce. We know that diversity in groups creates a better working environment and promotes creativity, something that is fundamental for our success. We welcome all applications. 
We go through applications continuously so don't wait - send in your application today!
In case of questions, please reach out to recruiting manager Michael Rosenberg at +46 46 272 1800

jobs.occupation: Associate researcher in Experimental lung transplantation
jobs.description:
Description of workplaceThe research group is led by Associated professor Sandra Lindstedt and has a long-standing interest in research related to lung transplantation, post-transplant complications, and lung regeneration. The group focuses on developing novel therapeutic strategies to treat lung injury, improve donor organ quality, and reduce complications following lung transplantation. A particular focus is on acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), primary graft dysfunction (PGD), and regenerative approaches to lung repair.
We offerLund University is a governmental authority, which means you get special benefits, generous holidays, and a favorable occupational pension. Read more on the university's website about being employed at Lund University, Work at Lund University
Work descriptionA associate researcher position is available within the Lindstedt research group, focusing on translational research in lung transplantation, lung injury, and regenerative medicine. The duties at the research unit primarily consist of experimental and laboratory-based research, with a particular focus on the development and evaluation of novel therapeutic strategies to improve lung repair and transplantation outcomes.
The main responsibilities include:
independently designing, planning, coordinating, and conducting research projects, as well as collecting, analyzing, interpreting, and managing experimental data.
The work involves the development and optimization of experimental protocols, evaluation of therapeutic interventions, and application of cellular, molecular, ultra-high-plexed immunofluorescence and histological techniques to investigate mechanisms of lung injury, repair, and regeneration.
The position also includes responsibility for preparing high-quality scientific manuscripts for publication in international peer-reviewed journals, contributing to research grant applications, and presenting research findings at national and international scientific conferences.
The majority of the work will be conducted independently, while also involving close collaboration with internal and external research partners and clinical collaborators.
In addition, the position includes mentorship and supervision of doctoral students, Bachelor’s and Master’s students, and other junior researchers, as well as contributing to the coordination and development of ongoing research activities within the group.

Other work tasks might also be included.
QualificationsRequired qualifications
PhD (or equivalent) in biomedical sciences, biotechnology, molecular biology, regenerative medicine, or a related field.
A minimum of four years of documented research experience following completion of the PhD, demonstrating scientific independence and responsibility.
Documented experience in experimental and translational biomedical research, particularly within cell therapies, lung injury, lung transplantation, or regenerative medicine.
Hands-on experience with small and large-animal models and/or ex vivo organ perfusion.
Experience with standard cellular and molecular biology techniques, including cell culture, ELISA, Western blotting, qPCR, immunohistochemistry and high-plexed immunofluorescence.
Demonstrated ability to independently design, plan, coordinate, and conduct complex experimental research projects.
Documented scientific productivity through publications in international peer-reviewed journals.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.
Independent and responsible, with the ability to organize and manage research activities and take responsibility for scientific quality and project progress.
Collaborative, with strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work effectively in interdisciplinary research environments.
Analytical and solution-oriented, with the ability to critically evaluate experimental results and address complex scientific challenges.

Meritorious qualifications:
Additional specialized training in experimental transplantation, regenerative medicine, cell therapy, or related disciplines.
Relevant training and certification in laboratory animal science, particularly involving large- and small-animal experimental models.
Completed courses in higher education teaching and pedagogy.
Experience with experimental lung transplantation, including large- and small-animal models of lung injury and transplantation.
Hands-on experience with ex vivo lung perfusion (EVLP) and human ex vivo lung models, including precision-cut lung slices (PCLS).
Experience in the development and evaluation of cell-based and regenerative therapies, particularly mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) and mitochondrial therapeutics.
Experience with cellular, molecular, histological, and proteomic analyses, including the handling and processing of human and animal tissue samples.
Experience in managing and coordinating interdisciplinary research projects and national or international collaborations.
Documented experience in scientific supervision, preparation of research grant applications, and dissemination of research findings through publications and international conferences.

Other information
The position is a fixed-term employment according to the Special Fixed-term Employment (SÄVA) regulations §5 p1 LAS, and it is full-time. The desired start date is 2027-01-01 or as agreed upon, with an end date of 2027-12-31.
How to Apply
Applications are to be submitted via the University’s recruitment system. The application should include a CV and a personal letter justifying your interest in the position and how it matches your qualifications. The application should also include a degree certificate or equivalent and any other document to which you would like to draw attention (copies of grade transcripts, details of referees, letters of recommendation, etc.).

jobs.description:

Company Description

Bosch Home Comfort in Tranås develops, manufactures and sells advanced heat pumps that harness energy from nature’s own resources: rock, water and air. Our Tranås site brings together manufacturing, research and development, and business functions, creating an environment where ideas and decisions are closely connected to our products and operations.
We believe in technology that makes a difference: Invented for life.
 

Job Description

Your contribution to something big
Do you enjoy understanding what really drives performance in a manufacturing business, rather than simply reporting the numbers?
As our Plant Controller, you will work at the intersection of finance and manufacturing, partnering closely with Plant Management and colleagues across production, logistics, engineering and other functions.
You will turn financial and operational data into insights that support better decisions, stronger performance and continuous improvement. This is a hands-on controlling role where you can build a broad understanding of our manufacturing operation and have a real impact on how we manage costs, investments and performance.
Your key responsibilities
Business partnering: Act as a financial partner to Plant Management and cost center owners. Provide analysis, challenge assumptions and translate financial performance into clear insights and actions.
Planning & forecasting: Drive key parts of our business planning, budgeting and forecasting processes, including cost centers, Capex, production volumes, headcount and product costs.
Manufacturing performance: Analyze manufacturing costs, productivity and operational deviations. Work with the organization to understand root causes and identify appropriate countermeasures.
Product costing: Lead Planned Product Cost (PPC) calculations, follow Actual Product Costs (APC) and analyze the operational and financial drivers behind deviations.
Investments, assets & inventory: Support investment planning and follow-up, fixed asset management, inventory valuation, physical stocktaking and continuous inventory control.
Reporting & continuous improvement: Drive monthly and annual plant performance reporting while continuously improving our processes, reporting, dashboards and use of SAP and other digital tools.

Qualifications

What distinguishes you
You have a degree in Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, Industrial Engineering and Management, or a comparable field, together with experience in controlling, financial analysis or a related finance role.
Experience from manufacturing or another industrial environment is particularly valuable.
We are looking for someone with:
Strong analytical skills and confidence working with financial and operational data
Experience with budgeting, forecasting, cost accounting or operational reporting
Good knowledge of Microsoft Excel
Experience working with ERP systems. SAP experience, particularly within controlling or manufacturing processes, is an advantage
Professional working proficiency in English, both written and spoken. Swedish is an advantage, but not a requirement

Experience with product costing, Power BI, automation or other data-analysis tools is an advantage, but you do not need to tick every box. We value your ability to learn, understand the business and turn data into meaningful insights.
Who you are
You are curious about the business behind the numbers. When you see a deviation, your instinct is not simply to report it. You want to understand why it happened, what is driving it and what we can do about it.
You are comfortable asking questions, challenging assumptions and collaborating across functions to find solutions. You can explain financial concepts clearly to colleagues outside Finance and combine strong analytical thinking with a practical mindset.
You take ownership of your work, build strong relationships and are motivated by understanding how a manufacturing business works and how Finance can help make it better.

Additional Information

Why join us in Tranås?
In Tranås, more than 600 associates work across manufacturing and research & development of innovative heating solutions for a more sustainable future.
For a Plant Controller, this creates an exciting environment where you can see the connection between the numbers, the decisions and what actually happens in the factory.
The role gives you broad exposure to manufacturing finance, product costing, investments and operational performance, while working within the international Bosch organization. It is an opportunity to deepen your controlling expertise, influence the business and continue developing your career.
At Bosch, we value openness, trust and different perspectives, and we want our associates to have opportunities to grow both professionally and personally.
What we offer
Competitive compensation
Pension, insurance and other benefits in accordance with our collective agreement
Flexible working hours and hybrid working possibilities where compatible with the role
Employee discounts on Bosch products
Development opportunities within an international Bosch organization

Regular presence at our Tranås site is an important part of the role because of the close collaboration with our manufacturing organization.
If you enjoy combining finance, manufacturing and problem-solving, we would like to hear from you.

jobs.occupation: Mechanical Design Engineer - Active with Kids
jobs.description:
Bring your life 
Are you passionate about developing products where safety, engineering excellence, and user experience come together? Are you excited about developing innovative, safe, and functional solutions for families who love outdoor adventures? If you're driven by the challenge of designing products that combine cutting-edge technology with the highest standards of safety and comfort for children, then this is the perfect opportunity for you! 
As part of our Active with Kids category, you'll contribute to solutions that combine thoughtful design, engineering excellence, and industry-leading safety. With an exciting product portfolio and roadmap ahead, you'll help to shape the next generation of strollers that make adventures with kids safer, easier, and more enjoyable. 
 
What you'll do at Thule 
As a Mechanical Design Engineer - Active with Kids, you'll be part of our committed engineering team specifically developing strollers. Together, we take ideas from concept to finished product through a structured and collaborative development process. 
In this role, you will design and develop components in CAD, create high-quality technical specifications, and collaborate closely with engineering colleagues, project managers, simulation and test engineers, and prototype specialists to solve technical challenges and ensure every detail meets the high standards and requirements. 
You will take an active role in ordering and evaluating prototypes, analyzing test results, and using simulations to verify the strength and performance of your designs. 
In addition, you will document technical solutions, manage design-related risks, and contribute to engineering best practices. Leading and supporting design reviews will be an important part of your role, helping ensure our products meet the highest standards of safety, quality, and sustainability. 
 
What you bring 
To succeed in this role, we believe you have a university degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related field, combined with some years of experience in mechanical design and product development. 
You have worked with a variety of materials and understand how to optimize designs for functionality, durability, and safety. Experience from consumer products, the automotive industry, or other safety-critical applications is highly valuable. You have experience working with plastic components and understand their manufacturing processes. You are fluent in both Swedish and English. 
As the role includes practical elements, we believe you thrive in a hands-on product development environment. As a person, you are self-driven, structured, and solution-oriented, with the ability to turn ideas into robust and well-engineered products. You are a team player who enjoys collaborating across disciplines and can effectively manage multiple projects and priorities simultaneously. 
 
Why you should join Thule 
At Thule, we are Proud to Be Thule. We believe anything is possible when we stay curious, take initiative and challenge ourselves. We encourage everyone to take ownership and make the most of their part of the business. 
We believe we win as a team by collaborating across functions, sharing knowledge and supporting one another. United by our passion for our products, the outdoors and the Thule brand, we take pride in what we do and create a culture where everyone contributes, grows and has fun. 
 
Hiring Process 
Apply by submitting your application and resumé through “Apply for position” on our Thule Career Site. The application deadline is December 6, 2026.

We look forward to hearing from you! 
Thule is a global sports and outdoor company. We offer high-quality products with smart features and a sustainable design that make it easy for people across the globe to live an active life. Under the motto Bring your life — and with a focus on consumer-driven innovation and long-term sustainability — we develop, manufacture and market products within the product categories Sport & Cargo Carriers (roof racks, roof boxes and carriers for transporting cycling, water and winter sports equipment, and rooftop tents mounted on a car), Active with Kids & Dogs (car seats, strollers, bike trailers, child bike seats and dog transport), RV Products (awnings, bike carriers and tents for RVs and caravans) and Bags & Mounts (backpacks, luggage and performance mounts).
Thule Group has about 3,000 employees at nine production facilities and 35 sales offices worldwide. The Group’s products are sold in 138 markets and in 2025, sales amounted to SEK 10,4 billion.

Develop and maintain Clinical Evaluation Plans and Clinical Evaluation Reports

Conduct systematic literature reviews and critically assess clinical data and scientific evidence

Evaluate clinical safety, performance and benefit-risk, integrating evidence from risk management, verification and validation, usability and other relevant activities

Support regulatory submissions and interactions with notified bodies

The chance to influence how clinical evaluations are conducted at Cambio and contribute to the continued development of our clinical strategy

 About you
You have a strong scientific and analytical mindset and are comfortable working with complex clinical information and turning it into clear, well-founded conclusions.

Experience working with clinical evaluation of medical devices, either leading or contributing to the clinical evaluation process

Experience working with the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR) and relevant guidance documents

Experience in systematic literature reviews and critical appraisal of clinical and scientific data

Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English and good communication skills in Swedish

jobs.occupation: Technical Project Manager  R&D & China Production
jobs.description:

Aluwave is a Swedish technology company specializing in customized LED lighting solutions. We work with product development, industrialization and manufacturing in an international environment, with operations and partners in Europe and Asia.
About the role
We are looking for an experienced Technical Project Manager – R&D & China Production to coordinate product development, industrialization and manufacturing activities between Sweden and China.
The role combines technical project management with hands-on engineering, supplier development, quality management and cost optimization. You will work closely with our organization in Sweden and with electronics manufacturers and suppliers in China, supporting products from development and industrialization through production ramp-up and continuous improvement.
The position requires a strong technical understanding of electronics manufacturing as well as practical experience of working with the Chinese manufacturing and supplier environment.
