Transport is at the core of modern society. Imagine using your expertise to shape sustainable transport and infrastructure solutions for the future. If you seek to make a difference on a global scale, working with next-gen technologies and the sharpest collaborative teams, then we could be a perfect match. 
The role:
As an Occupational Health and Safety Engineer at Volvo Construction Equipment in Arvika, you will play a key role in leading, developing and challenging the business in the areas of occupational health and safety. You will enable us to strengthen the factory’s long-term health and safety efforts, guided by our principle of Safety First.
You will work in a manufacturing environment with complex production flows and a wide range of roles, which calls for a proactive and systematic approach to occupational health and safety. We offer a role that combines strategic and operational work, with a clear focus on development, change management and continuous improvement.
The role involves a broad range of contacts, at different levels across the organization and with external parties such as authorities and neighboring businesses. You will also be an important member of our Core Values network. This is a varied role in which you will lead and develop occupational health and safety work in Arvika in line with Volvo Group’s guidelines.
You will monitor legislation and regulations relating to occupational health and safety, keep the organization informed of changes, and act as the contact person for authorities on these matters. You will train, engage and follow up with the business to ensure compliance with legislation and regulations and support continuous improvement.
You will also support risk assessments, investigations into serious incidents, and take part in local and global forums across the Volvo Group.
You will join a small, committed team where you will have plenty of opportunity to make an impact. The role offers a high degree of independence and personal responsibility, alongside close collaboration with colleagues, managers and other functions. You will drive occupational health and safety issues, processes and development work forward, supported by a skilled network and an engaged manager. You will have the opportunity to combine strategic development with hands-on support to the business, helping create a safe and sustainable workplace for the future.
Who are you?
We are looking for someone with a university degree in occupational health and safety, or other education or experience that we consider equivalent. You have several years of experience in professional occupational health and safety work, preferably in an industrial environment. You have a strong knowledge of occupational health and safety legislation, regulations and authority requirements. Experience leading people is an advantage.
You communicate fluently in both spoken and written Swedish and English, as the role involves many local and global contacts.
You are proactive and capable of seeing both the details and the big picture. You thrive in environments that are fast-paced and demanding—settings where you are encouraged to draw upon your full range of personal and professional capabilities. People listen to you because you bring facts, analysis, and proposed solutions to the table.
Experience with and a good understanding of ISO 45001 are considered an advantage. You are well placed to succeed in this role if you collaborate easily, work in a structured and systematic way, and show initiative and perseverance when facing challenges. It goes without saying that you are strongly motivated to help create a safe workplace where safety always comes first. In addition to your skills and experience, we will place great importance on your personal suitability for the role.
This is a full-time position based on-site in Arvika. Some travel may be required as part of your contribution to Volvo Group’s occupational health and safety network and community.
Ready for the next move?
As part of the recruitment process, a background check as well as alcohol and drug testing may be conducted. You will be informed if applicable. Last day to apply is November 22. The recruitment process is on-going, so don´t wait to apply.
In case you have questions about the position, contact Stefan Wingskog at stefan.wingskog@volvo.com or Julia Strandman at julia.strandman@volvo.com
We value your data privacy and therefore do not accept applications via mail. 
Who we are and what we believe in 
We are committed to shaping the future landscape of efficient, safe, and sustainable transport solutions. Fulfilling our mission creates countless career opportunities for talents across the group’s leading brands and entities.
Applying to this job offers you the opportunity to join Volvo Group. Every day, you will be working with some of the sharpest and most creative brains in our field to be able to leave our society in better shape for the next generation. ​We are passionate about what we do, and we thrive on teamwork. ​We are almost 100,000 people united around the world by a culture of care, inclusiveness, and empowerment. 
Part of Volvo Group, Volvo Construction Equipment is a global company driven by our purpose to build the world we want to live in. Together we develop and deliver solutions for a cleaner, smarter, and more connected world. By unleashing everyone’s full potential, we build a more sustainable future for all our stakeholders. Come join our team and help us build a better tomorrow.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral researcher in Mechanical Engineering within Gear Technology
jobs.description:
We are looking for a postdoctoral researcher in Mechanical Engineering for a two-year fixed-term position at the School of Science and Technology.
Subject area
The subject area for this position is Mechanical Engineering with a focus on Gear Technology.
Background
A postdoctoral researcher will be affiliated with the group of Mechanical Engineering within the School of Science and Technology and will conduct research as part of the KKS project ‘Applying advanced mechano-chemical surface treatment for optimizing gear production process’. Specific areas of interest are Gear Tribology Testing, Contact Surface Simulation, and Gear Manufacturing. The current research project aims to study several technologies together to develop an optimized heat and surface treatment approach for production of high-load vehicle gears. A mechano-chemical surface treatment with combined change of surface chemistry, hardness and roughness is to be developed and integrated into existing methods to enhance gear performance with minimal environmental footprint and reduced production time and cost.
Duties and responsibilities
The appointment as a postdoctoral researcher is intended to enable persons who have recently been awarded their doctoral degree to consolidate and develop primarily their research skills. Besides consolidating their research and publication track, the postdocs may be required to contribute to the departmental duties (e.g., via teaching at the undergraduate or graduate level), up to 20 % of their time.
Qualifications
Those qualified for appointment as a postdoctoral researcher are applicants who at the time of appointment hold a doctoral degree or have a degree from abroad deemed to correspond to a doctoral degree in a relevant area. Applicants with doctoral degrees that have been awarded no more than 3 years prior to the application deadline are to be considered first. The applicant may not previously have held a position as a postdoctoral researcher for more than one year in the same subject and at the same higher education institution. The position is for a term of 24 months according to agreement with the successful candidate. If the person during the period of employment has been on parental leave, the period of employment is to be extended by the corresponding number of days. The period of employment may also be extended in the event of absence due to illness.
Assessment criteria
A basis for the assessment is the applicant’s ability to disseminate research information and communicate through high-quality publications. In addition, the applicant’s suitability for the position will be assessed. Suitability refers to the applicant demonstrating the personal qualities required to successfully perform the duties and responsibilities at hand, the ability to cooperate with other members of staff, and the ability to contribute to the development of the operations. A successful applicant should demonstrate strong interpersonal skills, the ability to work collaboratively with colleagues from diverse backgrounds, and a commitment to respectful and ethical professional behaviour.
Particular attention is to be paid to the applicant’s prospects of contributing to the future development of both research and education. Importance is also attached to a demonstrated ability and ambition to embark on a career within academia.
A successful applicant should:
Be autonomous and show strong and independent problem-solving skills and critical analytical abilities,
Demonstrate a strong background and publication track record within gear technology area, preferably with knowledge of tribology testing, manufacturing and surface treatment simulation. A background in relevant simulation techniques is also given weight when considering candidates.
Have a passion for research in advanced topics for the development of gear manufacturing and surface treatment.

Information
This is a full-time position for two years. At Örebro University, salary depends on the successful candidate’s qualifications and experience. The expected starting date is April 1st, 2027, or as agreed.
For more information about the position, contact Dr. Omar D. Mohammed, e-mail: omar.mohammed@oru.se. For administrative matters, contact Dr. Jens Ekengren, e-mail: Jens.Ekengren@oru.se.
At Örebro University, we expect each member of staff to be open to development and change; take responsibility for their work and performance; demonstrate a keen interest in collaboration and contribute to development; as well as to show respect for others by adopting a constructive and professional approach.
Örebro University actively pursues equal opportunities and gender equality as well as a work environment characterised by openness, trust and respect. We value the qualities that diversity adds to our operations.
Application
The application is made online. Click the button “Apply” to begin the application procedure.
For the application to be complete, the following electronic documents must be included:
Cover letter (1 page), describing your research interests, explaining why you are interested in this project, why you would be a good fit for the position, and how you could contribute to the continued development of Örebro University
CV with a relevant description of your overall qualifications and experience
Account of research qualifications and experience
Copies of relevant course/degree certificates and official transcripts as well as references verifying eligibility and criteria met
Relevant scientific publications (maximum of 10 and in full-text format)

Only documents written in Swedish, English, Norwegian and Danish can be reviewed.
More information for applicants will be found on our career site: https://www.oru.se/english/career/available-positions/applicants-and-external-experts/
The application deadline is November 23, 2026. We look forward to receiving your application!
As we have already made our choices in terms of external collaboration partners and marketing efforts for this recruitment process, we decline any contact with recruitment agencies and advertisers.
As directed by the National Archives of Sweden (Riksarkivet), we are required to deposit one file copy of the application documents, excluding publications, for a period of two years after the appointment decision has gained legal force.

Strategic Research is a central function at Alleima supporting all product areas through long-term research and innovation. With decades of metallurgical expertise and a commitment to innovation, we are seeking a passionate and forward-thinking R&D Specialist to join our New Alloys team. Together, we combine deep metallurgical knowledge with advanced research methods to develop the next generation of stainless-steel materials.  We run projects from a lean product development standpoint, focusing on knowledge building. After reaching proof of concept, the projects are handed over to product development for a large-scale ramp-up.
Are you passionate about materials research and development and eager to contribute to the next generation of advanced stainless-steel materials? You might be the person we are looking for. Apply today!
Placement: Sandviken
Your Role
As an R&D Specialist in the New Alloys team you will be part of a group with deep knowledge from several different technical areas important for successful alloy development such as advanced material characterization, thermodynamic modelling, corrosion science, powder metallurgy, and hot working. The strength of the team lies in combining our skills, sharing knowledge, and working together in an open and collaborative atmosphere. 
Your task is to participate in, lead, and identify alloy development projects, knowledge-building pre-studies, or other investigations in line with Alleima’s strategic research plan. You deliver results according to agreements and present your research in an accurate and structured manner through e.g. internal technical reports, project meetings, and steering group meetings. You will be an important contact person for material development and represent Alleima in external research projects in collaboration with institutions and universities. 
Since our projects and assignments are based on technical requirements from both external customers and our internal organization, an important part of the role is to collaborate and communicate with multiple stakeholders, and build strong, long-term relationships.
About you
We are looking for someone with a Master of Science (MSc.) degree or a PhD in Materials Science, Materials Engineering, Technical Physics, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field, combined with several years of industrial research experience within the stainless-steel industry, preferably in product or process development of high-alloy stainless steels or nickel-based alloys. Previous project management experience, particularly in alloy development, is advantageous.
You bring in-depth expertise in one or more areas relevant to alloy development. This may include production processes, such as casting or hot-working and their limitations and possibilities related to alloy development, product requirements and knowledge such as high-temperature corrosion, wet corrosion or mechanical properties related to stainless steel materials in demanding environments. 
You are familiar with common characterization techniques used in materials development, such as LOM and SEM, and have a solid understanding of the relationship between microstructure and material properties
We value your passion and personality characterized by your analytical and problem-solving mindset. As a person, you are structured, thorough, and driven, with the ability to identify opportunities, critically evaluate results, and see projects through to completion. In a determined and independent manner, you plan and drive the work forward but are flexible when the situation requires it. Your communicative and collaborative manner allows you to easily share your competencies and results with the rest of the team. All in all, you are a person who can do both hands-on technical work and move projects forward in a pedagogical and inclusive way. You have excellent communication skills, both verbally and in writing, preferably in both Swedish and English as we operate in an international environment.  
What you can expect from us
At Alleima, you will be part of a global organization where collaboration, curiosity and continuous development are at the heart of what we do. We believe that diverse perspectives and an inclusive workplace help us make better decisions, create new opportunities and grow together.
Our values guide us in everything we do: We Care, We Deliver and We Evolve. Together, we take responsibility, challenge ourselves to improve and support each other in making a difference.
Additional information
In connection with employment, alcohol and drug tests are carried out according to our procedures for a safe working environment and a background check might be conducted.
For more information regarding the position, contact:
Christina Haraldsson, Recruiting manager, +46 70 524 95 70
For more information regarding the recruitment process, contact: 
Frida Carlsson, Recruitment Specialist, +46 73 599 76 14
Union contacts:
Maria Sundqvist, Akademikerföreningen, +46 70 651 73 81
Kjell-Åke Klockervold, Ledarna, +46 70 314 24 43
Stefan Jonsson, Unionen, +46 70 396 03 00
You are welcome to submit your application no later than 2026-11-22.
About us
At Alleima, our mission is much more than delivering high-quality products, technology, and processes - working together to develop solutions based on our customer's needs and thus achieve our business goals, is a better way to describe our daily work. With curious employees and safety as our priority, we create a work environment where you can develop both personally and professionally.
With a clear direction for our journey ahead, utilizing our position as a technology leader, progressive customer partner, and sustainability driver, we aim to become an even stronger company in our industry.
Are you ready to take on this challenge together with us? Join us on our journey! www.alleima.com

What we do at Blykalla
Blykalla is a Swedish deep-tech company at the forefront of the nuclear industry, pioneering the development of small modular reactors that provide clean, safe, and reliable energy. Thanks to lead-cooling, we achieve high safety in a very compact format, allowing for a simple and cost-effective design that can be mass-produced. Our unique reactor design will provide safe and green baseload energy that perfectly complements solar and wind power.

What you’ll get to do
We are seeking a Senior Control Systems Engineer with deep expertise in ABB 800xA DCS to lead the development of Blykalla's plant control system architecture and implementation strategy.
This is a unique opportunity to help define the control philosophy of a first-of-a-kind advanced nuclear reactor. You will play a key role in ensuring that Blykalla develops and retains ownership of critical control system intellectual property while working closely with ABB and other suppliers.

Key Responsibilities
DCS Architecture & Ownership
Lead the design and development of Blykalla's plant-wide automation and control system architecture.
Define the ABB 800xA system architecture for reactor, balance-of-plant, auxiliary, and test facility applications.
Develop internal engineering standards, libraries, templates, and control strategies to maximize in-house ownership of intellectual property.
Establish long-term governance for control system design, lifecycle management, cybersecurity, and configuration control.

Control System Engineering
Develop functional specifications, control narratives, cause-and-effect matrices, and automation philosophies.
Design and implement control logic, sequences, interlocks, alarms, and operator interfaces.
Configure ABB 800xA applications, controllers, engineering environments, and HMI systems.
Define communication architectures including OPC UA, IEC 61850, Modbus, Profibus/Profinet, Ethernet/IP, and other industrial protocols.
Develop and maintain simulation and testing environments for control system validation.

Nuclear Plant Integration
Support the integration of reactor systems, safety systems, and balance-of-plant equipment into the overall control architecture.
Work closely with reactor, thermal-hydraulic, electrical, mechanical, and safety engineers to define system requirements.
Contribute to licensing and regulatory documentation related to instrumentation and control systems.
Support development of digital I&C architectures aligned with nuclear industry expectations and international standards.

Vendor & Stakeholder Management
Act as the primary technical interface with ABB regarding 800xA architecture, licensing, engineering tools, and implementation support.
Ensure that Blykalla retains ownership of application software, engineering databases, configuration standards, and control strategies.
Manage external engineering partners and system integrators where required.
Participate in factory acceptance tests (FAT), site acceptance tests (SAT), commissioning, and startup activities.

Verification & Validation
Develop testing methodologies for control logic verification and system validation.
Lead integration testing and commissioning activities.
Support development of digital twins and operator training simulators.
Ensure traceability from requirements through implementation and testing.

Who you’ll get to work with
The Senior Control Systems Engineer sits in the Plant engineering Team within Blykalla. We are a diverse team that is passionate about our work and Blykalla. 
Who you are
You will be part of a highly skilled team with a can-do attitude. We value personnel chemistry and strive to create a workplace where you enjoy coming to. There are however a few things that we think will help in order for you to succeed in this role, these are:
MSc or BSc in Control Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Automation Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, or related discipline.
Minimum 10 years of experience in industrial automation and control systems engineering.
Extensive hands-on experience with ABB 800xA DCS engineering, configuration, commissioning, and lifecycle management.
Proven experience designing and implementing large-scale DCS architectures.
Experience developing control strategies for complex industrial facilities.
Strong understanding of industrial networks, field instrumentation, and process control.
Fluent in English, spoken and written
Fluency in Swedish is a plus

Technical Skills
Expert-level knowledge of ABB 800xA:
AC 800M controllers
Control Builder
Aspect Objects
System 800xA Engineering
Operator Workplace
Alarm Management
Batch and Advanced Process Control (desirable)
Strong understanding of:
ISA-88
ISA-95
IEC 61511
IEC 61508
Industrial cybersecurity principles
Configuration management and software lifecycle practices
Experience with simulation and testing environments.

Location 
This position is for our office in Stockholm.

Reference & Background Checks
As part of our recruitment process, we conduct background checks on all candidates. We may also conduct reference checks to gain a well-rounded understanding of your professional experience, performance, and ways of working. This includes both references provided by you and, where relevant, conversations with other professional contacts who have worked closely with you. We strive to be transparent about our reference-checking process and handle all personal data in accordance with applicable data protection regulations. Any additional references will be sought with professional judgment and only when considered relevant to the role.
We offer competitive compensation aligned with our internal salary framework and growth potential in the role.
We do not accept applications via email. 
We are not open to external help from recruitment agencies.
 
Note on AI Use: Blykalla may use AI technology to assist with certain administrative aspects of the hiring process, such as note-taking, interview documentation, and reporting. However, every resume and application is reviewed directly by our recruiting team. AI tools are used solely for operational support and do not influence candidate evaluation or hiring decisions.
Öppen för alla
Vi fokuserar på din kompetens, inte dina övriga förutsättningar. Vi är öppna för att anpassa rollen eller arbetsplatsen efter dina behov.

jobs.occupation: Social Producer - Organic Social & Creator Marketing
jobs.employer_name: H & M Hennes & Mauritz GBC AB
jobs.description:
Job Description
WHAT YOU’LL DO 
As Social Producer, you’ll take ownership of social and creator-led productions from brief to final delivery. You’ll turn creative ideas into clear, effective production plans and bring together the right creators, talent, production partners and suppliers to make them happen. 
Working across both fastmoving social content and larger campaign activations, you’ll create flexible production set-ups that allow ideas to come to life at speed without compromising quality or creative intent. You’ll be an important link between creative development and execution, helping ensure our content is relevant for the platform, audience and brand. 
Key responsibilities include 
Lead end-to-end production of social-first and creator-led content, from brief and planning to final asset delivery. 
Translate creative concepts into clear and actionable production plans while protecting the original creative vision. 
Source, negotiate with, contract and manage creators, talent, production partners and other external suppliers. 
Plan and book productions, managing budgets, timelines, contracts, resources and deliverables. 
Manage both smaller, agile creator-led productions and larger social campaign activations. 
Partner closely with creative teams to anticipate production needs and enable strong creative decision-making. 
Ensure content and assets are produced with relevant social platforms, formats and requirements in mind. 
Build flexible and scalable production approaches that support both planned and reactive content creation. 
Continuously identify new partners, production models and ways of working that improve efficiency, speed and relevance. 
Proactively identify and solve production challenges while maintaining a smooth process for everyone involved. 

WHO YOU’LL WORK WITH 
You’ll work closely with creatives and other colleagues across social and creator marketing, turning creative concepts into high-quality content and executions. You’ll also collaborate with creators, talent, agencies, production partners and suppliers, acting as a key connection between creative ambition and production delivery.  
This is a collaborative role where you’ll need to build strong relationships while feeling confident taking ownership and moving productions forward independently. 
WHO YOU ARE 
You’re an experienced producer who knows how to bring creative ideas to life. You combine strong production expertise with an understanding of social content, creators and the realities of producing content for fast-moving digital channels. 
You don’t need every answer from day one. What matters is that you have strong production judgement, understand what a creative idea needs to succeed and know how to find the right people and solutions to make it happen.  
We are looking for people with… 
Strong experience in content production, with relevant experience producing social-first, digital or creator-led content. 
Proven experience independently managing productions from brief through to final delivery. 
Experience working directly with creators, talent, production partners and suppliers. 
Experience with sourcing, negotiation, contracting, budgets, timelines and production planning. 
An understanding of social platforms and how production requirements can differ across channels such as TikTok and Instagram. 
The ability to translate creative concepts into practical production plans without losing the creative intent. 
Strong stakeholder management and collaboration skills. 
An understanding of how to balance creative ambition, commercial considerations, quality, speed and efficiency. 

 And people who are… 
Independent and comfortable taking ownership from start to finish. 
Highly organized, solution-oriented and able to manage several moving parts at once. 
Curious about social media, creator culture and evolving ways of producing content. 
Collaborative and strong at building relationships across creative and commercial teams. 
Flexible and comfortable working in a fast-moving environment where not everything is defined from the start. 
Confident challenging established ways of working and exploring new production models. 
Equipped with strong creative judgement and an eye for culturally and socially relevant content. 

WHO WE ARE 
H&M Group is a global company of strong fashion brands and ventures. Our goal is to prove that there is no compromise between exceptional design, affordable prices, and sustainable solutions. We want to liberate fashion for the many, and our customers are at the heart of every decision we make. 
We are made up of thousands of passionate and talented colleagues united by our shared culture and values. Together, we want to use our power, our scale, and our knowledge to push the fashion industry towards a more inclusive and sustainable future. 
WHY YOU’LL LOVE WORKING HERE 
At H&M Group, you’ll be part of an international and collaborative environment where your ideas and perspectives matter. Alongside opportunities to learn, develop and build your career across H&M Group, we offer a range of benefits. 
Your H&M Group benefits include: 
Employee discount: As an H&M Group employee, you receive an employee discount across eligible H&M Group brands, in stores and online where applicable. Brands include H&M, H&M HOME, H&M Move, COS, Monki, Weekday, & Other Stories and ARKET. 
H&M Incentive Program (HIP). 
Wellbeing allowance: Employees in Sweden receive an annual wellbeing allowance, supporting activities that contribute to health and wellbeing. 

JOIN US 
Our uniqueness comes from a combination of many things - our inclusive and collaborative culture, our strong values, and opportunities for growth. But most of all, it’s our people who make us who we are. 
Take the next step in your career together with us. The journey starts here. 
This is a permanent position based in Stockholm, Sweden. Apply as soon as possible by submitting your CV and portfolio in English. 
Due to data privacy regulations, we only accept applications through our career page. 
We are committed to a recruitment process that is fair, equitable, and based on competency.We therefore kindly ask you to not attach a cover letter in your application.

jobs.occupation: Head of Enterprise and Platforms Nordics to Dintero
jobs.description:
Are you an experienced payment sales professional ready to combine commercial leadership with closing strategic deals yourself? Dintero is looking for a Head of Enterprise & Platforms Nordics to bring together its Nordic enterprise sales efforts, develop the team and drive growth across some of the company’s most important customer segments.
About the job
This is a direct recruitment, which means that the recruitment process takes place through Bravura and you are employed directly by Dintero.
About the company
Dintero is a fast-growing Norwegian fintech company challenging traditional payment providers with a modern, fully integrated payment platform. The company is one of few players in the Nordics covering the entire payment value chain and is licensed to process Visa and Mastercard transactions directly, making Dintero Norway’s first new acquirer in more than 20 years.
The offering covers online and in-store payments, Unified Commerce and payment solutions for platforms and marketplaces. With enterprise customers such as Vy and regulatory approval to offer payment services across the EEA, Dintero is positioned for further expansion across the Nordics and Europe. In 2025, the company onboarded more than 2,100 new businesses, increased payment volume by over 150% and revenue by 200%, while reaching profitability in Q4.
You will join a growing Nordic organisation with short decision paths and a high degree of ownership. There are established structures and processes, but these evolve as the business grows. Leaders are expected to identify what can be improved and actively contribute to developing how the organisation works.
Tasks and responsibilities
As Head of Enterprise & Platforms Nordics, you will have commercial responsibility for developing Dintero’s enterprise and platform sales across Sweden, Norway and Denmark. A key part of the role is to bring the three markets together and establish a common Nordic approach to sales, pipeline management and commercial priorities.
This is a player-coach role, particularly during the first year. Alongside leading and developing the team, you will personally work with Dintero’s most strategic customers and drive complex enterprise opportunities from initial dialogue to signed agreement. You will work with senior and C-level decision-makers and navigate longer sales cycles involving both commercial and technical stakeholders.
You will also develop the existing sales team and play an active role in recruiting and building the team further across the Nordics, with the ambition to hire 3–5 additional salespeople during the first 12 months. As the organisation expands, the role will gradually shift towards more leadership and commercial strategy, while maintaining a strong connection to customers and the market.
You will work closely with the CEO, product and technical teams to develop Dintero’s enterprise offering. You are not expected to be a technical specialist, but you need to understand complex payment solutions and be comfortable discussing areas such as APIs, integrations and platform architecture.
Your main responsibilities include:

Lead and develop Enterprise & Platforms sales across the Nordics

Personally drive and close strategic enterprise and platform deals

Coach and develop the existing sales team and recruit additional salespeople

Develop structure around pipeline, sales methodology, CRM and forecasting

Collaborate with leadership, product and technical teams to develop the enterprise offering

Education, experience and personal characteristics
Several years of experience within the payments industry

Proven experience closing complex, high-value enterprise deals in the Nordic market

Previous leadership experience, including people responsibility, coaching, developing and recruiting salespeople

Experience selling both in-store terminal solutions and online/e-commerce payments

Commercial and technical understanding of areas such as APIs and integrations and platform architecture

Existing network within Nordic enterprise retail

Fluent English and at least one Scandinavian language: Swedish, Norwegian or Danish

Experience selling through and building partnerships with e-commerce platforms and integration partners is meritorious

An existing network across marketplace or platform verticals is meritorious

To succeed in the role, you take ownership and are comfortable creating structure while remaining close to sales. As a leader, you coach and give experienced salespeople ownership of their deals while setting clear expectations around execution and results.
You are comfortable in an environment where processes evolve as the company grows. Rather than simply working within an existing structure, you identify what could work better and take initiative to change it. You are also curious and able to quickly understand complex technical and commercial topics, even when you do not have all the answers from the start.
Other information
Start: Upon agreement  Location: Stockholm, Oslo or Copenhagen. If based outside Oslo, regular travel to the Oslo office is expected.  Salary: Upon agreement

We use a competency-based recruitment approach in all our recruitment processes to ensure fair and unbiased selection. We also review applications on an ongoing basis, which means that the job posting may be closed once we have received a sufficient number of applications.
If your profile matches the role, we will contact you for an initial phone interview. Regardless of whether you progress further in the process, you will receive feedback on your application.
Do you have any questions? Feel free to contact us!
📧 info@bravura.se 📞 010-171 47 10
We recommend submitting your application as soon as possible, as applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis.
We look forward to receiving your application!
#Specialist

Ovako is one of Europe’s leading manufacturers of advanced engineering steel and has supplied steel for critical industrial applications for nearly 500 years. The company is now making a strategic investment in the defence industry and is looking for someone who wants to play a key role in establishing and developing Ovako’s position in one of Europe’s fastest-growing segments.
At Ovako, you will have the opportunity to combine business development, an understanding of the defence industry and relationship building in a role offering substantial autonomy, high visibility and the opportunity to shape the direction of an entirely new initiative. You will join a stable industrial company with a long-term perspective, Nordic production, strong ownership and a clear ambition to grow within the defence segment.
The location is flexible, although we would ideally like you to be based at our sales office in Karlskoga. You may also be based at one of our major production sites in Hofors, Smedjebacken, Boxholm or Hällefors, or at our office in Örebro.
In the role of Sales Manager Security and Defense, you will be responsible for establishing, developing and strengthening Ovako’s business within the defence industry. This is a newly created role designed to develop Ovako’s long-term position throughout the defence supply chain, from OEMs and systems suppliers to subcontractors and other key players in the segment.
At the heart of the role is identifying business opportunities at an early stage, building relationships with the right decision-makers and creating a strong pipeline of future defence business. You will take a strategic approach to mapping the market, projects, decision-making processes and material requirements, while moving commercial discussions forward through customer meetings, quotations, negotiations and long-term relationship development.
To succeed, you need to be comfortable with long sales cycles. You understand how the defence industry operates, know where decisions are made and can build trust with technical specialists, procurement professionals and business leaders alike. The role requires a high degree of independence, and you will be expected to set your own agenda, take the initiative and drive business forward, even when results may take time to materialise.
You will represent the full Ovako Group offering and work closely with the sales organisation, business units, production and R&D to translate customer needs into long-term business opportunities.
We are looking for someone with an established network within the defence industry and existing relationships with relevant players, such as OEMs, systems suppliers, subcontractors or companies in related defence industries. You have experience in sales, business development, procurement or engineering within the defence sector and are accustomed to navigating complex business environments where sales cycles are often long and involve multiple stakeholders.
Experience in the steel industry is an advantage, but what matters most is your understanding of the defence segment, its decision-making processes and how to build long-term business through trust and relationships. Experience in steel, component manufacturing, materials engineering or the manufacturing industry is desirable but not essential.
As a person, you are commercially driven, persistent and proactive. You thrive in a role where you can establish structures, identify opportunities and move activities forward on your own initiative. At the same time, you bring a strategic perspective and the ability to understand the connections between different players throughout the defence supply chain. You naturally build trust, work in a structured way and are motivated by developing business that creates lasting value.
A good command of Swedish and English, together with a category B driving licence, is essential for the role. Ideally, you hold a university qualification in a relevant field or another post-secondary qualification. Travel is part of the role. The location is flexible, although we would ideally like you to be based in central Sweden or be able to visit one of Ovako’s sites regularly.
You will be offered a unique opportunity to help build Ovako’s defence industry initiative from the ground up. The role has strong support from management and Group management and gives you the opportunity to make your mark on a business area of major strategic importance to the company.
Ovako combines the resources of a large industrial company with a culture where individuals make a difference. You will have autonomy and responsibility, strong support from colleagues and the opportunity to influence both the development of the business and your own professional growth. You will join a global organisation with strong industrial owners, Nordic production and a long tradition of innovation, quality and sustainability.
We welcome your application today. Applications are reviewed and interviews conducted on an ongoing basis. Please submit your application below, as we do not accept applications through any other channel. If you would like to learn more about the role, please contact Made for Sales.
About Ovako
Ovako is a leading European manufacturer of engineering steel for customers in sectors including industry, energy, mining and automotive, as well as defence-related applications. The company has approximately 2,500 employees, annual revenue of approximately EUR 1 billion and production facilities in Sweden and Finland. Drawing on extensive industrial experience, strong materials expertise and a clear focus on sustainability, Ovako develops advanced steel solutions for some of the world’s most demanding applications. The company is part of the Nippon Steel Group through Sanyo Special Steel and has a long-term industrial owner with a strong focus on innovation and future growth.

About us
Danieli Morgårdshammar AB is part of the international Danieli Group and has been serving the Nordic metals industry for more than 170 years. Based in Smedjebacken, Sweden, we support steel, aluminum and other metal producers throughout Scandinavia with engineering services, spare parts, technical support and long-term partnership solutions.

We operate in an industry where trust, competence and personal relationships are often more important than presentations, marketing materials or corporate references. Our success is built on credibility and on being recognized as a reliable partner by the people who operate and maintain production facilities every day.
 
Responsibilities
We are looking for an experienced industry professional who already understands the reality of steel mills, rolling mills and metal processing plants.
This is not a typical sales position, more a business developer position.
The ideal candidate is someone who has worked directly within the metals industry or closely alongside plant personnel and understands how industrial decisions are truly made. Candidates coming directly from steel, aluminum or other metals production facilities are particularly encouraged to apply.
The primary focus of this role is the development of Danieli aftermarket and service business.
Activities include the sales, coordination, and follow-up of the following services and solutions for your designated customers:
Spare Parts Supply
Technical Services
On-site Assistance
Maintenance Support
Roll Shop Solutions
Equipment Refurbishments
Small and Medium Revamping Projects
Plant Modernizations and Upgrades
Engineering and Technical Consulting

Success in this role requires the ability to understand customers' operational challenges and identify opportunities where Danieli's technical expertise and service capabilities can create measurable value.
Technical Requirements
We are particularly interested in candidates who have:
Previous experience in the steel, aluminum or metals industry.
Direct experience working in or closely with production plants, rolling mills, maintenance organizations or technical departments.
Existing professional relationships within the Nordic metals industry.
A strong understanding of industrial operations, maintenance and production environments.
Experience interacting with: Roll Shop Managers; Production Managers; Maintenance Managers; Foremen and Supervisors; Category Managers; Purchasing Departments; Technical Specialists.

More than technical qualifications, we are looking for someone who understands plant culture, speaks the language of industrial operations and can quickly establish credibility with the people who influence purchasing decisions.
Fluent English, written and spoken, mother language Swedish.
Willingness to travel throughout the Nordic countries.
Valid driving license.
Experience with CRM systems (but not as a primary focus)
Technical education or equivalent industry experience is considered an advantage.

Soft Skills
For this position, interpersonal capabilities are just as important as technical knowledge.
The successful candidate will:
Build trust naturally and quickly.
Be highly relationship-driven and people-oriented.
Communicate confidently with personnel at all organizational levels.
Be proactive, decisive and commercially minded.
Feel comfortable opening doors and creating opportunities from scratch.
Demonstrate strong ownership and initiative.
Possess the credibility and character required to earn customers' confidence over time.
Be capable of transforming an initial contact into a long-term business partnership.

In the Nordic business culture, trust is often the primary factor behind purchasing decisions. We therefore place exceptional importance on integrity, credibility and relationship-building skills.
Other
Danieli - Morgårdshammar and the Danieli Group are already well known throughout the Nordic metals industry. Significant efforts have been made in recent years to increase our presence within production facilities, establish direct contacts with key stakeholders and strengthen our reputation across the region.
Several customers already work with Danieli. However, substantial opportunities remain to deepen those relationships and expand our involvement far beyond our current level of business.
Your mission will be to transform existing awareness into trust, and trust into long-term partnerships, customer loyalty and sustainable business growth.
We are looking for someone who can become the person our customers call first when they need advice, support or a reliable partner.
The successful candidate will not operate as a stand-alone salesperson.
Commercial strategy, customer development plans and growth initiatives are defined in close coordination with the Danieli Group headquarters in Italy and the Nordic Area.
The role is fully integrated within a broader international organization and supported by dedicated technical, commercial and engineering resources worldwide.
Daily support is provided by the Nordic Area Manager, while customer visits and business development activities are frequently performed jointly with Product Line Managers, technical specialists and senior representatives from Danieli headquarters.
The objective is to combine local presence and relationship-building with the engineering expertise, product knowledge and global resources of the Danieli Group. We are therefore looking for a person who enjoys being on the front line with customers, while being fully supported by an international team behind them.
You are not expected to be a lone hunter searching for orders.
We are looking for someone who can walk into a plant, understand the challenges faced by its people, speak their language and ultimately become the person they trust when it is time to place an order.
In the Nordic industrial culture, trust is not a sales tool, It is the foundation upon which long-term business is built.
Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and the position may be filled before the closing date. Interviews are conducted continuously throughout the recruitment process. Preferred start date is as soon as possible, but this is not a requirement.
Morgårdshammar AB is a member of Teknikföretagen and applies the relevant collective bargaining agreements within the Swedish engineering industry, including the Technology Agreement (Teknikavtalet).

jobs.occupation: Volvo Group Graduate Program 2027 - Supply Chain Developer
jobs.description:
Company description:
This is the Volvo Group Graduate ProgramA new era of manufacturing and R&D is here. Are you passionate about technology, eager to solve real business challenges, ready to drive innovation, and join our transformation journey? Then this Graduate program is for you!As part of the Graduate Program at Volvo Group, you will tackle real challenges from day one and contribute to the development of next-generation production solutions.The 15-month Graduate Program combines 50% time in your home department with 50% dedicated program activities, giving you broad exposure across Volvo Group. Through local and international rotations, short-term assignments and targeted training in areas such as operations, engineering and purchasing, you will build a strong understanding of our business, brands and strategy.
Job description:  Your future teamService Operations & Technology (SOT) is the engine behind customer uptime and service growth in the Volvo Group. Within the Trucks Technology & Industrial Division (TTI), we bring together engineering, purchasing, logistics, remanufacturing and technology into one global end-to-end organization. We are more than 5,000 colleagues across 50+ sites worldwide and we work close to our customers and markets to deliver reliable, high-performance service solutions that keep vehicles and machines running. 
 In our region Gent&Eu within SOT, we operate the Inbound and Outbound service market flows of spare parts. Our team is responsible for the Inbound flow, from order call-offs to our material suppliers through to arrival at the central distribution center. We work cross-functionally with all the great team members in the inbound supply chain. Our daily collaboration covers suppliers, operational planning, purchasing, engineering, remanufacturing and the central distribution center. We believe that the best results are achieved together, while having fun! Are you like us and want to join the journey to secure high customer satisfaction? Then this might be just the perfect role for you.
 How you’ll contributeThe aim of your role is to ensure that we continuously develop our Supply Chain in line with the Volvo Group ambitions. You will, among others, lead and coordinate cross-functional improvement initiatives, create structure, alignment and momentum across stakeholders.You will facilitate workshops, working groups and knowledge-sharing forums where different perspectives are brought together. Also, you will practice leadership through influence by clarifying objectives, engaging others, following up on commitments and supporting change. Our sites and operational work lie across Europe and as you will be located in Gothenburg Sweden, traveling within Europe will occasionally be required.
 Who are you?We are looking for someone with a strong transformation and collaborative mindset who is eager to learn, explore and understand the business. You thrive in dynamic environments, embrace new challenges and ambiguity and take ownership of your own development and growth.
 With strong analytical skills, you take initiative and drive tasks forward with determination while bringing fresh perspectives and innovative ideas to the team. You enjoy building relationships and leveraging a global network to create impact while working collaboratively across teams and functions. In addition, you contribute to a culture of continuous learning by actively sharing knowledge, exchanging insights and supporting the development of others.As this is a graduate position, we value your potential, learning agility and motivation to grow. We are interested in candidates who see leadership as part of their future career. What matters to us is your curiosity about how data, automation and digital solutions can improve the way we work and create lasting business value. We want you to be part of exploring and shaping what comes next.
 To qualify for the Graduate program
  You have completed a bachelor or master’s degree prior to the start of the program but not more than three years ago
 Should not have more than three years' full-time relevant working experience in the field prior to starting, excluding part-time work during studies
 Have relevant education within Supply Chain, Logistics, Engineering or project management is required
 You have experience in Supply Chain-related work, such as logistics and warehousing, production, project management and understanding of data, system and application
 You are fluent in English, both written and verbal
 You are willing to travel and participate in international short-term assignments
  
Additional desirable skills
  Fluent in Swedish and Flemish
  
What’s in it for you?Our Volvo Group Graduate Program starts in August 2027 and you will be offered a permanent position at Volvo TTI SOT Gent&Eu with placement in Sweden, Gothenburg.
 These are some of the benefits of joining our program:
  An opportunity to work with the latest technology.
 An exciting and global working environment with experienced colleagues.
 Possibility to gain international experience through a short-term assignment abroad.
 A competitive salary and a permanent position from day one.
 Various workshops and seminars designed to help you grow into your future career at Volvo Group.
 The possibility to shape your own career with endless career opportunities.
  
The application processThe journey begins! An email confirmation will be sent when you submit your application. After this, it is still possible to update your personal profile by logging into your account. The hiring team will review your application together with the hiring manager. Shortlisted candidates will be contacted with information about the following steps.
 Last day to apply: 22nd of November 2026 
  As part of the recruitment process, a background check as well as alcohol and drug testing may be conducted. You will be informed if applicable.

Welcome to SSC Space (formerly Swedish Space Corporation), the perfect workplace for those passionate about technology in general and space in particular. 
With space organizations, research institutes, institutional and commercial actors as customers, we offer specialist expertise in satellite communications, spacecraft consulting services, rocket and balloon systems, and much more. 
SSC Space also has one of the world’s largest global networks of ground stations for satellite communications. We own and operate the Esrange Space Center in Kiruna, northern Sweden, with the aim of launching satellites in the near future. 
Are you fueled by a passion for people and the ambition to create an awesome workplace? Are you ready to embark on an exciting journey with us to help Earth benefit from space? 
If you answer yes to these questions, we invite you to seize the opportunity to make a significant impact as optical communications engineer in our team. We are looking for a dedicated person who shares our core values of Customer passion, Care, Collaboration, Curiosity, and Courage. 
As an Optical Communications Engineer you will join our multidisciplinary optical team and contribute to developing satellite data services based on free-space optical communications. You will support system development, integration, testing and operational deployment, working across ground stations, spacecraft interfaces and customer missions.

REQUIREMENTS
MSc (or equivalent background) in aerospace engineering, engineering physics, electrical engineering, optical communications or a related field.
Experience in system engineering methods (requirements, interfaces, verification) and end-to-end system thinking. 
Ability to perform system-level analysis, requirements analysis and trade-offs.
Proven ability for problem solving, working with conflicting deadlines both individually and in a team environment to achieve program goals, with ability to prioritise work and deliver clear documentation (such as technical reports) on time. 
Fluency in English, both written and spoken.
Applicants must be legally allowed to work in the EU and hold a European citizenship. Swedish citizenship is an advantage. Evidence of eligibility will be required from candidates as part of the recruitment process.

In addition, experience with free-space optical communication systems, space systems and ground segment architectures, as well as RF or optical link budget and performance analysis is highly beneficial. Knowledge of network protocols and distributed system architectures is also considered an advantage. You should be able to work effectively both independently and in collaboration with others.

RESPONSIBILITIES
In your role as Optical Communications Engineer you are responsible for supporting the development, integration, and demonstration of SSC Space’s optical ground network services, contributing to both operational deployment and future service development. You operate within the Optical Program and support ongoing projects such as demonstration missions, ground station development, and network integration, while also exploring new applications such as deep-space optical communications and quantum technologies and providing technical support to the business developments. 
The main responsibilities include performing in-depth technical analyses of optical communication systems, including link performance and operational requirements, site surveys and environmental assessments, orbit analysis and mission geometry, end-to-end system and subsystem testing and network integration.  
The role also entails collaboration and interactions with internal and external partners and participation in technical discussions, workshops and project meetings, as well as on-site work of the SSC Space optical ground stations at the OGS sites (e.g. Australia and Chile) on occasion. Documentation and reporting of the work, tests and outcome are a part of the general responsibilities of the role.

BENEFITS
We offer you 
A unique opportunity to contribute to a wide range of projects and play an active role in both the Swedish and international space industry.
An excellent opportunity for personal and career development.
An exciting, international workplace characterized by an open atmosphere and proud employees all over the world. 

Additional benefits 
In addition to vacation and traditional public holidays, we offer extra paid leave throughout the year, such as time off between Christmas and New Year, Ascension Day, amounting to 6-11 extra days depending on the calendar. 
Wellness allowance of SEK 5,000 per year.
Health benefits such as voluntary health insurance and regular health checks for eligible employees. 
Access to a benefit bike through a tax-efficient leasing program.
Support for employee-driven activities that promote connection, health, and culture across teams.
Collective Agreement, including good pensions plans, parental pay and insurance.

 
LOCATION
This is a full-time, permanent position based at our office in Solna. 

NEXT STEP 
If this opportunity sparks your interest, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible! We review applications continuously and will conduct interviews throughout the process. 
When applying, please include your CV. While you are welcome to include a brief personal note or letter, our evaluation will primarily focus on your skills and qualifications as outlined in your CV, ensuring a fair and unbiased recruitment process. 
As part of our recruitment process, all candidates selected for employment undergo a background check and security screening. 
 
WE HELP EARTH BENEFIT FROM SPACE
SSC Space is a leading global provider of advanced space services, with more than 50 years of experience. We help space organizations, research institutes, commercial and institutional actors from all over the world to get access to space. 
With local presence on all continents and about 800 committed employees, we offer specialist expertise in satellite communications and satellite control services, spacecraft operations, rocket and balloon systems, launch services and flight test services, as well as engineering, operations and consultancy services for space missions. 
 We help Earth benefit from Space. Learn more at sscspace.com

We are looking for an experienced AI Backend Engineer to build the core intelligence layer of a fast-scaling AI company backed by NVIDIA, Microsoft, and AWS.
About Antrino
Antrino Labs is building the platform that makes every square meter intelligent.
The physical world runs on processes nobody can actually see. Goods move, machines idle, space goes unused, and decisions about all of it are based on samples, guesses, and reports written after the fact. Antrino lets any organization deploy vision intelligence into a physical space and get back what is actually happening there, as structured, real-time information it can act on. Not a research project or a custom integration, but a platform where you describe what matters and deploy it.
We have grown from 6 people to a team of 28 in less than a year, closed our Seed round, announced together with Dagens Industri, and are registered with Inspektionen för strategiska produkter (ISP), the Swedish authority for strategic and dual-use products. Everything we build follows Privacy by Design.
The role
You will build the services that turn a customer's intent into working intelligence.
When a customer builds something in Studio, our composition canvas, that graph has to become a running system: a plan that decides which models to call, in what order, gated by cost and confidence, and that produces events and evidence a customer can trust. You will work on the compiler that turns the graph into an execution plan, the runtime that executes it, and the Python and TypeScript services that detection, classification, and measurement run through.
You will also work on our Agent, which interviews customers, proposes and edits these graphs, and deploys them with confirmation. Getting an LLM to reliably manipulate a structured graph, validate it, and explain its reasoning is a real engineering problem, not a prompting exercise.
The role sits between the team building our first-party detection models and the engineers building the product interface. It is backend systems engineering for a product whose core logic is built out of AI calls.
What you will work on
Backend services for detection, classification, and measurement, largely in Python with FastAPI
The compiler that turns a Studio graph into an execution plan, and the runtime that deploys and runs it
Routing logic that decides which model handles which work, including cost gating where a cheap model decides when an expensive one runs
The Agent's interview, graph-editing, and deployment flows that turn natural language into a working pipeline
Integrating our first-party detection models, and frontier model APIs where they do something ours do not yet, behind one clean interface
Turning raw model output into structured, auditable events and evidence an operator can trust
APIs and data models for streams, behaviors, runs, and events in PostgreSQL with row-level security
Tests and evaluation harnesses for logic that includes non-deterministic model calls
Debugging production issues that span a customer request, our orchestration, and the model call underneath

Our stack
You do not need experience with all of this, but you should recognize most of it and be able to argue about it.
Backend: Python, FastAPI, TypeScript, Node.jsData: PostgreSQL through Supabase, with row-level security, 
Streaming: RTSP ingestion, RTSP→HLS conversion, live and archive pipelines
Infrastructure: Azure, GitHub Actions, on-site compute reached over Tailscale
Who we are looking for Substantial backend experience on production systems, ideally where an LLM or ML model was part of the core logic rather than a bolted-on feature
Strong Python, and comfort in TypeScript or Node.js
Real experience designing APIs, data models, and service boundaries, including PostgreSQL
Experience building with LLM APIs beyond a chat wrapper: tool use, structured output, agentic flows, or a model as one step in a larger pipeline
An understanding of how to test systems with non-deterministic components
Experience with real-time or streaming data is a strong advantage
Excellent written and spoken English. Swedish is a plus, not a requirement

You can reason about a graph or compiler-shaped problem even if you have never built a compiler. You make decisions with incomplete information, take responsibility for the outcome, and say so clearly when something you built was wrong.
Life at Antrino
You will join a team of driven, ambitious people who thrive at a fast pace and enjoy working together. We go to AI events, host our own, and end plenty of weeks with an afterwork. You will work closely with our engineers in Stockholm and our growing team in Bangalore.
What we offer
Direct access to the founders, the engineering team, and customers
Real ownership of a core layer of the platform rather than delegated tickets
Potential participation in our stock option programme after the probationary period
Hardware of your choice
AI events, afterworks, team activities, and travel when the business requires it
Occupational pension, insurance, and friskvårdsbidrag

Process
Introductory conversation about your background and the role
Technical conversation about systems you have built and why you made the decisions you made. No whiteboard algorithm puzzles
Working session with the engineering team on a real problem from our stack
Conversation with the founders about options and terms

We review applications continuously. References may be requested at the final stage.
Apply with your CV and, if you have one, a link to something you have built. A repository, a shipped product, or a short note about a system you are proud of tells us more than a cover letter

Looking for a flexible part-time job alongside your studies or other commitments? Do you enjoy helping people, keeping things organized, and making a workplace feel welcoming? Then this might be the perfect role for you!
We're looking for a friendly and proactive Office Manager to take care of our Framna office in central Östersund.
Become part of the team
At Framna, we create digital products used by millions of people every day. But great products start with great people, and we believe a welcoming and well-functioning workplace makes all the difference.
Our Östersund office is home to a creative bunch of colleagues working with technology, design, and digital products. We also share our space with other companies, so there's always a mix of people around.
As our part-time Office Manager, you'll be the go-to person for the little (and sometimes bigger) things that keep the office running smoothly. You'll work independently in Östersund, with support from our Office and People team in Stockholm and Kalmar.
This is a 20% position, making it a great opportunity to combine with university studies or other commitments. We'll agree on a schedule together that works for both you and the needs of the office, giving you flexibility in how you spread your hours throughout the week. And if you're a student, you're more than welcome to stay and study at our office when you're not working!
What you will do
Your main mission is simple: make sure our office is a great place to be!
Some days you'll be making sure we have everything we need, other days you'll be helping organize an event or solving an unexpected office issue.
More specifically, you will be:

Making sure everyday office essentials are in place, from coffee and milk to printer supplies and other necessities.

Keeping the office welcoming, organized, and running smoothly, including taking care of plants and shared spaces.

Being the main contact person for our tenants and helping with practical questions and requests.

Coordinating with external suppliers and partners, such as cleaning services and property management.

Handling practical office administration, including access systems and coordinating checks of safety equipment.

Helping plan and organize local events, breakfasts, afterworks, and other fun activities.

Working closely with colleagues in Östersund and our Office team in other Framna studios.

Who you are
You don't need years of experience or an impressive CV to succeed in this role. What matters most to us is your attitude, your ability to take initiative, and your willingness to help others.
We believe you might feel at home with us if you:

Are friendly, service-minded, and enjoy making other people's day a little easier.

Are organized, reliable, and good at noticing what needs to be done.

Like taking initiative and finding practical solutions.

Feel comfortable working independently while staying connected with colleagues.

Enjoy meeting different people and creating a welcoming atmosphere.

Communicate comfortably in both Swedish and English.

Previous experience in service, administration, hospitality, or a similar role is a plus
Whether you're a university student looking for a flexible job or simply someone who enjoys making things run smoothly, we'd love to hear from you!
About Framna 
Framna means ‘to bring forward’ in Old Norse. And that is exactly what we do. We partner with industry leaders (and those about to be) to create excellent digital products that define markets, reshape industries, and deliver meaningful impact.
Born from the union of digital agencies Bontouch, Move, and Shape, Framna emerged from a strong, product-led culture. Today, over 600 of us collaborate across 11 studios in Denmark, the Netherlands, Poland, Sweden, Switzerland, and the US.
Every day, millions of users around the world rely on the products we help shape. From seamless payments to daily commutes, from better health management to smarter shopping. Our work supports more than €150 million in daily transactions and consistently earns an average App Store rating of 4.5.
Together with some of the world’s most ambitious brands, including Essity, SJ, Swish, SEB, and Vattenfall, we craft products that lead markets and push boundaries. Because when products win, businesses win. We call it Win by product.
What you get 
A flexible part-time role. We'll agree on a schedule together, making it easier to combine work with studies or other commitments.

An office to call your own. A welcoming workplace in central Östersund, where you're also welcome to stay and study outside your working hours.

A chance to make a difference. You'll play an important part in making everyday office life easier and more enjoyable for everyone.

Great colleagues. Friendly, creative people who enjoy spending time together and helping each other out.

Freedom and responsibility. We trust you to take initiative, organize your work, and find smart ways to make things run smoothly.

Our hiring process
We like to keep things simple:

Short introductory call

Interview

Reference check

The position is based at our office in Östersund, Sweden. This is an on-site role, with working hours planned together based on the needs of the office and your availability.
We're reviewing applications on a rolling basis, so don't wait to apply. We look forward to learning more about you!

About XBP Europe 
XBP Europe is an innovative, forward-thinking provider of bills and payment process solutions. Leveraging an EMEA-wide footprint and proprietary technology and services, we are backed by decades of industry-relevant experience.

Bills and payment processes are increasingly omni-channel and paperless. That’s where XBP Europe comes in. Our offerings enable seamless workflows and frictionless transactions. XBP Europe combines physical documents, digital data, and instant messaging to help organisations work smarter. As part of that, we help to gather, process, and refine valuable data for use in decision-making.

Our digital transformation solutions enhance efficiency, cash flow, and end-user experience. We serve a growing client list throughout Europe. See why organisations of all sizes choose XBP Europe as a digital transformation partner, visit our website at www.xbpeurope.com

Individual Development Plan and Career Growth

Lyten is leading an industrial revolution through Lyten 3D Graphene™, a breakthrough supermaterial unlocking a new generation of products — from lithium–sulfur batteries and energy storage systems to concrete admixtures, lightweight composites, and next-generation sensors that are revolutionizing industries. Together, these innovations are making a massive global improvement and driving real-world impact across energy, mobility, construction, and defense.
At Lyten, we believe the most meaningful careers begin with purpose — and with people who want to make a difference. We’re not just developing advanced supermaterials — we’re about to change the world as we know it, reshaping how energy is stored, how products are built, and how progress is made.
We’re entering an exciting growth phase, scaling production across the U.S. and Europe and expanding our team of engineers, scientists, and innovators.

Director of Manufacturing Engineering
Job Scope
As Director of Manufacturing Engineering, you will lead and grow the team responsible for developing and industrialising the manufacturing solutions required for Lyten's next-generation battery technologies. You will play a key role in bridging technology development and industrial execution, ensuring future products can be successfully scaled into robust, efficient, and high-quality manufacturing processes.
This is a strategic leadership role with significant influence on technology decisions, industrialisation strategy, manufacturing concepts, and future production capabilities. A key focus will be on growing the organisation while working closely with R&D, Product Development, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, and external partners to build the manufacturing platform that supports Lyten's future growth.
By helping transform breakthrough technologies into scalable manufacturing solutions, you will play a direct role in enabling the energy transition and strengthening Europe's industrial future.

Key Responsibilities
· Lead, develop, and grow the Manufacturing Engineering organisation.
· Build a high-performing culture with clear roles, responsibilities, and ways of working.
· Drive the industrialisation of next-generation products, processes, and manufacturing technologies.
· Collaborate with R&D, Product Development, Operations, Quality, and Supply Chain to ensure manufacturing readiness.
· Shape manufacturing strategy, technology roadmaps, and future production capabilities.
· Evaluate and implement new manufacturing concepts, automation solutions, and production technologies.
· Drive operational excellence, continuous improvement, and long-term capability development.
· Build strong relationships with suppliers, partners, and key stakeholders.
Requirements
· Degree in Engineering or a related technical discipline.
· Extensive experience within manufacturing engineering, industrialisation, production engineering, or advanced manufacturing.
· Proven leadership experience building, developing, and leading engineering organisations.
· Strong track record of scaling manufacturing operations and industrialising new products, technologies, or manufacturing concepts.
· Experience leading managers, engineers, and multidisciplinary teams in complex environments.
· Background from automotive, industrial equipment, electronics, battery, or other advanced manufacturing industries.
· Strong strategic mindset combined with the ability to execute and deliver results.
· Experience working across international and cross-functional organisations.
· Excellent stakeholder management, communication, and influencing skills.
· Fluent in English, written and spoken.
Who You Are
You are a mature and inspiring leader who builds trust, develops people, and creates high-performing teams. You understand that lasting success comes through empowering others and enabling teams to perform at their best
You have a holistic perspective and naturally see the bigger picture. You understand how engineering, technology, operations, and business decisions are interconnected and consistently act in the best interests of the wider organisation.
You combine strategic thinking with a practical approach to execution. Comfortable navigating complex challenges, you can identify priorities, make sound decisions, and deliver results through others. You take ownership, work independently, and drive initiatives forward with structure and purpose.
We place great importance on personal qualities
Why Work at Lyten

Job description:

At Robotto, we build advanced autonomy and software solutions for drones and unmanned systems. Our work brings together computer vision, embedded software, control, electronics and real-world product development.We are looking for an Embedded Software Engineer with strong C++ experience to develop software close to the hardware layer of our drone platform. Contribute customer and market insights to Xenergic’s commercial direction, value proposition and product priorities together with the CEO, CTO and Engineering Manager.

Extensive international travel is an important part of the role, with approximately 100 travel days per year expected, primarily to customers, partners and key semiconductor markets in North America, Asia and Europe.

In this recruitment, Xenergic is collaborating with Nexer Recruit. For questions about the role or the recruitment process, contact Johanna Värmfors at johanna.varmfors@nexergroup.com or +46 730 821 230, or Artan Bitiqi at artan.bitiqi@nexergroup.com or +46 723 61 28 44.
