TL;DR
You're a communications professional who can plan and execute the work that advances Lovable's objectives across EU and Swedish policy environments, making sure our voice is heard on the issues that matter most. You'll pair sharp corporate communications with real policy fluency — working closely with internal teams and external partners to help policymakers, media, and other stakeholders understand Lovable's perspective on the key files and issues that shape the environment we operate in.
This is a balanced role, equal parts policy operator and corporate communicator. You'll report to the European Communications and Public Affairs Lead.
Why Lovable?
Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.
We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.
Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.
What you'll do
This role makes sure Lovable has a credible, constructive voice in the rooms that matter — building a presence worth listening to and developing clear positions that reflect what Lovable actually builds and believes.
Advocate Lovable's positions on key policy files. You'll build and run our engagement with policy representatives across EU and Swedish institutions.
Own corporate communications on policy issues. Statements, briefings, op-eds, speaking moments, and the proactive announcements that build credibility over time. You'll develop the strategy, write the materials, manage media relationships, and make sure each piece reinforces the others.
Track the regulatory agenda and turn it into a point of view. You'll monitor the files that affect us and develop clear positions that reflect the company's reality and ambitions.
Build coalitions and work through industry. You'll represent Lovable in trade associations and industry groups, finding shared causes that move issues forward.
Act as a comms and policy partner to our cross-functional team. You'll work closely with the communications and cross-functional teams in preparing for engagements with policymakers, institutions, and press, strengthening the company’s voice in the European AI debate.
Who you are
You've operated in and around the policy world. That might mean an EU institution, a trade association, a think tank, or a public affairs firm. Wherever you've been, you know how a file moves from idea to law, and you can read the politics, formal and informal, that determine what actually happens.
You understand policy and can communicate it. You have experience from both policy work and corporate communications, and you're equally comfortable speaking to policymakers and media alike.
You can drive an issue forward in a complex political environment. You're comfortable with ambiguity and competing agendas, and you know how to prioritize when everything feels urgent.
You're a sharp writer with editorial judgment. You can turn a dense regulatory development into a crisp briefing, opinion piece or clean position statement.
You connect dots that other people don't see. You look at a piece of draft legislation and think ahead on what it means for the industry as well as what Lovable should say and to whom.
You're a genuine cross-functional collaborator. You work easily with cross-functional stakeholders, external partners, and coalitions. You don't wait to be invited into the room. You're not precious about who gets credit. You just make things work.
You're deeply curious about AI, technology policy, and the industry landscape. You keep up with what happens in the world instinctively — the news, the regulatory moves, the debates as they unfold. You understand where the conversation is heading well enough to spot a risk or an opportunity before someone hands it to you.
What you need to know
This is not a role where you set the strategy and hand off execution. You'll be writing the first drafts of our position statements, building the relationships and showing up in the room as a Lovable representative.
We move fast and plans change. The job runs on two clocks at once: you'll react to the urgent issue that lands today while building the relationships and positions that set us up for success in the long term. If you need a settled environment with predictable workflows, this will be frustrating. If you find that kind of pace energizing, you'll love it.
We're building public affairs and communications at a company that is itself being built. That means you'll have real influence over how this function develops in Europe: the positions, the relationships, the standards. That's the upside of being early.
Finally: joining Lovable Comms means you're deeply curious, data-driven, and not extremely precious about role boundaries. You find ways to work smarter with AI, to measure what matters, and to step into work that isn't technically "yours" when the moment calls for it.
About your application
Please submit your application in English. It’s our company language, so you’ll be speaking lots of it if you join.
We treat all candidates equally - if you’re interested, please apply through our careers portal.

Mycronic is a global high-tech company whose innovative solutions have been advancing electronics technology for over 40 years. Today we continue to grow and serve customers in an expanding variety of industries. What we do impacts the future of technology, and in turn, the way we live our lives tomorrow. We’re looking for people to join our talented, motivated and friendly team on the cutting-edge. Here, in an open, collaborative and flexible environment, you’ll work alongside leading industry experts and take on challenging projects that bring tomorrow’s electronics to life. If you have several years of work experience within software development and embedded systems and wants to be part of a growing company with world leading products, this is for you!
About the role
Mycronic has experienced strong growth in recent years, both organically and through acquisitions. With headquarters in Sweden, Mycronic is a global organization with subsidiaries, agents, and distributors in over 50 countries. Mycronic is divided into four divisions, and in this role, you will belong to PCB Assembly Solutions (PA). PA is a leading provider of equipment and solutions for surface mount technology (SMT) to electronics manufacturers who require rapid production adjustments while maintaining high efficiency. PA delivers systems for circuit board assembly, including both complete line solutions and individual systems for specific process steps, as well as advanced software for assembly process management and connected factories. In this role, you will be part of a team of 7 team members and collaborate with several functions across the company, such as architects, project managers and other software teams within for example AI.
You are offered
The opportunity to work in a multi-cultural company with knowledgeable, friendly and goal-oriented colleagues.
To work in an exciting company in a growth phase, where you can make a real impact in a fun and dynamic environment. Mycronic is a global company, yet small enough for you to truly make a difference.
The opportunity to work with world-leading products. The future of electronics production is increasingly complex. Denser boards, a wider range of miniaturized components, more NPIs and erratic production schedules. To address these challenges Mycronic has developed the industry’s fastest, most flexible and most precise jet printing and solder paste dispensing systems. Mycronic jet printing technology makes it possible to dispense solder paste for the most challenging circuit boards and components, with micrometer accuracy, maximum speed and perfect quality solder joints. Read more here: https://www.mycronic.com/product-areas/pcb-assembly/products/smt/jet-printing/.
Mycronic has a large software organization which will provide you with optimal opportunities to develop your knowledge in various areas of computer science – such as software architecture for robotics, machine learning, AI, optimization, and computer vision.

Work tasks
You will work in a broad developer role where you will truly have the opportunity to influence the final solution of the products. The Mycronic Jet Printer, which is the product area you will be developing the software for, includes electronics, mechanics, and software, creating exciting opportunities for those who want to work with complex software development involving multiple technical disciplines. We are continuously working to enhance our products; user-friendliness, particularly in terms of automation and user interfaces, which will also be part of your development work. Your primary focus will be on improving the products, with opportunities to contribute your ideas and collaborate as a team to create the best solutions. This may involve anything from adding capability features and reducing energy consumption to updating the GUI. Mycronic has both R&D, lab, and production in-house, meaning you will work close to the products you develop, which also gives you the opportunity to see the "real world" results of your work.
We are looking for
This is a role for someone with a strong background in software development and an interest in understanding the entire product and an ambition to grow into a software architect role. As a software developer you will have a key role in the product development since this is where all the technology in the machine comes together to provide the system functionality that meets the user. You will be involved in everything from requirements gathering to design, architecture and development and collaborate with several stakeholders. As a person, we see it as particularly important that you are goal- and detail-oriented and have strong collaboration skills. You also have a will to contribute with your ideas, and just like your colleagues, you always strive to develop yourself and contribute to the team´s collective growth. We expect you to make a strong contribution by adding new functionality, maintaining high quality and by helping to introduce new technology and processes to increase team efficiency.
You likely have:
A bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, electronics, mechatronics, or a similar field.
Strong software development experience with the capability and ambition to take on broader architectural responsibilities in a few years.
Knowledge in Java.
Strong knowledge of software development in Linux.
Experience of working with software systems that interact with embedded software and hardware.
Strong knowledge in English and good knowledge in Swedish (or have the desire to learn)

It is considered advantageous if you have: 
Knowledge in C and/or C++

Other Information
Start date: By agreement
Employment type: Permanent
Scope: Full-time
Location: Kista
Contact Information: Senior Recruitment Consultant Johanna Sörell, johanna.sorell@academicwork.se
The recruitment process is handled by Academic Work, and Mycronic requests that all questions regarding the process goes to Academic Work.

Our recruitment process
Problem-solving and personality test
Phone interview with Academic Work
In-depth interview with Academic Work
Interviews with Mycronic
Reference check + decision

Why Lovable?
Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.
We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.
Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.
What this role is and what it isn’t
It is a senior are lead role with scope. You’ll run an organization that spans product, platform, and applied AI - with other managers, senior engineers, and AI agents reporting in - and you’ll be accountable for what that organization ships, how it operates, and the business outcomes it drives.
It is still close enough to the work that you can drop into a Tech Lead role on a hard problem when the situation demands it. We don’t measure leadership IC time as a percentage. We measure it as the ability to pick up the work and ship at the bar you’re asking of your team.
It isn’t a role for managers who think of themselves as engineering-adjacent. You need to be credible in code, design, and on-call - and you need to want to be.
It isn’t a role for leaders who only think about engineering. We expect you to reason end-to-end about the business - economics, product, GTM, customers - and to make calls that are best for the company, not just best for your team.

What we’re looking for
15+ years of engineering experience, including 6+ years of people management at a pre-IPO startup, scale-up or frontier tech company, and at least 2 years of managing managers. Strong IC track record before management.
You’ve run an engineering organization of 30+ with managers and senior engineers reporting in. You can speak concretely about how you structured the org, how you hired up to that scale, and what you’d do differently.
Still hands-on at the Tech Lead level: you can pick up an unfamiliar codebase, design and ship a non-trivial change, run an incident, and review code at a high bar. You haven’t let your engineering muscle atrophy.
You’ve thought hard about humans and AI agents on the same team. What humans should and shouldn’t delegate. How productivity gets measured when the unit of work is shifting. Strong opinions, lightly held.
Comfortable navigating ambiguity and driving clarity at an organisational level, not just technically. You write the doc that aligns three teams instead of waiting for someone else to.
Deep technical credibility in at least one area - full-stack product (React/TypeScript + Go/Rust), platform and developer experience (Kubernetes, sandboxing, observability, CI/CD, application frameworks), or applied AI (training, evals, agent systems, model serving).
Cross-functional to your core and business-fluent: you work seamlessly across design, product, and go-to-market, and know how to bring people along with you; andable to reason end-to-end about unit economics, product strategy, GTM, and customer outcomes
Track record of building and growing teams: you’ve hired senior engineers others wanted to work with, grown managers under you who became great in their own right, and set up career growth and performance practices that didn’t require constant maintenance. People follow you between companies.
Based in Stockholm or London or ready to relocate — this is an on-site, 5-days-a-week role.

What you’ll do
In one sentence: Run the engineering organization that builds Lovable - humans and agents both - and stay close enough to the work to be the senior engineer in the room when it matters.
Lead engineering. Product, platform, and applied AI under one roof. Own the roadmap and the business outcomes the org is on the hook for.
Set technical direction across the org: drive the design docs and architectural decisions that span teams, push back hard on weak plans (including your own), and hold a high bar for what ships.
Shape engineering culture: how we ship, how we write code, how we hire, how we deploy agents. Set norms that outlast any single project.
Ship fast: at Lovable the question is always “how fast can we get this to users?” You bias toward production and pull research, prototypes, and experiments into reality on the order of days and weeks, not quarters.
Build the operating model for an engineering org where humans and AI agents work side by side. We’re inventing this in public, and you’ll set the patterns the rest of the company learns from.
Operate as a peer to the executive team. Own outcomes that span beyond engineering, make the company’s biggest calls alongside the rest of leadership, and translate them back into engineering work that matters.

Our tech stack
We’re building with tools that both humans and AI love:
Frontend: React, TypeScript
Backend: Go and Rust
Cloud: Cloudflare, GCP, AWS, many LLM providers
Data: ClickHouse, Firestore, Spanner, BigQuery
DevOps & tooling: Kubernetes, gVisor-based sandboxing for agentic workloads, GitHub Actions, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, Terraform
Local tooling: Nix, DevEnv

About your application
Please submit your application in English — it’s our company language, so you’ll be speaking lots of it if you join.
We treat all candidates equally — if you’re interested, please apply through our careers portal.

 Ready to join us?
Help us unlock human creativity and build the future of software creation.

jobs.occupation: Cyber Security Unit Manager - Cyber, Risk & Assurance
jobs.employer_name: H & M Hennes & Mauritz GBC AB
jobs.description:
Job Description

As Unit Manager for Cyber Risk & Assurance, you will lead H&M Group’s capabilities for cyber risk management, governance, compliance and assurance, playing a key role in strengthening the organisation’s security, resilience and ability to manage cyber risk in line with its risk appetite and regulatory obligations. 
As a member of the Cyber Security Leadership Team reporting to the CISO, you will share accountability for the overall cyber security strategy, priorities and long-term development of the Cyber Security function. Working closely with leaders across business, technology and cyber security, you will help shape outcomes that balance business objectives, security needs and risk management across H&M Group. 
You will provide strategic leadership for H&M Group’s Cyber Risk & Assurance capability, bringing together Cyber Security Frameworks, Supply Chain Security Risk and Security Control Assurance. Through your leadership, you will drive the continued evolution of cyber risk management and control assurance. 
WHAT YOU WILL DO
Lead the strategic direction, maturity and long-term development of H&M Group’s Cyber, Risk & Assurance capability, defining and evolving the strategy, roadmap and operating model in alignment with business, technology and cyber security objectives. 
Contribute as a member of the Cyber Security Leadership Team to the overall cyber security strategy, priorities and long-term capability development. 
Drive the continued development and maturity of the Information Security Management System (ISMS), including frameworks, policies and governance structures that enable consistent and effective management of cyber risk across H&M Group. 
Provide oversight and assurance of cyber security risks and controls, promoting transparency, accountability and effective risk-based decision-making. 
Strengthen H&M Group’s approach to security policy and compliance, regulatory requirements, security control assurance and governance reporting. 
Drive the continued development of third-party and supply chain security risk management, ensuring risks are identified, assessed and managed through effective governance and oversight. 
Lead budgeting, resource and investment planning, vendor strategy and prioritisation to support Cyber Risk & Assurance and wider cyber security objectives. 
Foster a high-performing, collaborative and inclusive culture focused on strong accountability, continuous improvement and business value. 

Leadership as a Unit Manager  
As a Unit Manager and member of the Cyber Security Leadership Team, you provide strategic leadership for your unit while contributing to the overall direction and development of the Cyber Security function. You develop high-performing leadership teams, drive organisational effectiveness and capability development. You demonstrate enterprise leadership by collaborating across the business, influencing senior stakeholders and supporting decisions that create value beyond your own unit. 
WHO YOU ARE
We are looking for someone with: 
8+ years of people management experience in cyber security, technology risk, governance, compliance, assurance or a closely related field. 
Proven experience leading enterprise-scale cyber risk, governance, compliance or assurance capabilities in a complex global organisation. 
Proven experience leading through managers and developing high-performing leadership teams, with accountability for a multidisciplinary organisation and its outcomes. 
Experience as a member of a senior cyber security, technology, risk or enterprise leadership team, contributing to shared strategy, priorities, investment decisions and organisational outcomes beyond your own area of responsibility. 
Strong knowledge of cyber security risk management, governance, compliance and assurance principles, methodologies and operating models. 
Strong knowledge of security frameworks, policies, standards and controls, and experience translating regulatory and internal requirements into effective security governance. 
Strong understanding of third-party and supply chain security risk management in complex global environments. 
Experience establishing meaningful cyber risk, governance and assurance metrics and translating risk and control information into clear business implications, priorities and decisions. 
Experience managing significant budgets, investments, resources, sourcing arrangements and external partners, including strategic vendor relationships. 
Excellent communication and influencing skills, with proven experience engaging senior and executive stakeholders and communicating complex cyber risk, regulatory and assurance topics in a clear and pragmatic way. 
Sound judgement and decision-making capability in complex, uncertain and risk-sensitive situations. 

 

Additional Information

This is a fulltime permanent role based in Stockholm, Sweden. 
If you believe your experience, skills, and ambitions align with this role, please submit your CV in English.
Diversity, Inclusion, and Innovation 
At H&M Group, we're deeply committed to fostering a Diverse & Inclusive environment. We actively seek out qualified candidates regardless of race, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religion, national origin, disability, or age. 
Our commitment to an inclusive workplace drives our dynamic and forward-thinking culture. Regardless of your background, origin, or preferences, your application is warmly welcomed. We value diverse perspectives and skills, and every applicant contributes to our vibrant, creative community. Join us and be part of the future we're building. 
Our Offer 
At H&M Group, you're not just joining a team – you're joining a value-driven culture and an expansive tech network. Enjoy perks like staff discount cards, flexible work arrangements, wellness benefits, parental support, and more. Here, you're encouraged to be yourself, experiment, and chart your own growth path. As you flourish, so do we, with opportunities to create tangible impacts and shape the future. 
WHO WE ARE​ 
H&M Group is a global company of strong fashion brands and ventures. Our goal is to prove that there is no compromise between exceptional design, affordable prices, and sustainable solutions. We want to liberate fashion for the many, and our customers are at the heart of every decision we make.​ 
​We are made up of thousands of passionate and talented colleagues united by our shared culture and values. Together, we want to use our power, our scale, and our knowledge to push the fashion industry towards a more inclusive and sustainable future. ​ 
​WHY YOU’LL LOVE WORKING HERE ​ 
We offer all our employees at H&M Group attractive benefits with extensive development opportunities around the globe. All our employees receive a staff discount card, usable on all our H&M Group brands in stores and online. Brands covered by the discount are H&M (Beauty and Move included), COS, Weekday, Monki, H&M HOME, & Other Stories, ARKET. In addition to our staff discount, all our employees are included in our H&M Incentive Program – HIP. You can read more about our H&M Incentive Program here. 
In addition to our global benefits, all our local markets offer different competitive perks and benefits. Please note that they may differ between employment type and countries. 
JOIN US​ 
Our uniqueness comes from a combination of many things – our inclusive and collaborative culture, our strong values, and opportunities for growth. But most of all, it’s our people who make us who we are.​ 
​Take the next step in your career together with us. The journey starts here.​ 
​ *We are committed to a recruitment process that is fair, equitable, and based on competency. We therefore kindly ask you to not attach a cover letter in your application.​

At Stegra, we’re not just building a plant, we’re proving that sustainable industry is possible. And to do that, we need people like you.
Join a team where safety comes first. Where we support each other, learn as we go, and make space for everyone to grow and contribute. This is your chance to be part of something big - while being closer to nature and leading a balanced, purposeful life.
Role Overview
Stegra is seeking a highly experienced and strategic Lead Legal Counsel – Project Finance to join our Legal team and take a leading role in supporting the company's large-scale project debt financing, together with related corporate and compliance work. This role will play a critical part in shaping and executing our debt financing strategy, ensuring compliance, and safeguarding the company’s legal and commercial interests across all debt-related matters.
Reporting to the Head of Legal – Corporate Finance & Company Secretary, and working closely and with support from the Corporate Finance Legal Counsel, you will take primary day-to-day ownership of the legal workstreams underpinning the company's large project financing package, including its ECA and public funding arrangements, multi-tranche lender structures, and security package.
This is an opportunity for an experienced, commercially-minded lawyer who wants to take ownership of a sophisticated and high-profile project finance capital stack, working directly with senior stakeholders on some of the company's most important legal and financial matters. The role carries substantial responsibility and autonomy, with significant scope to shape how project finance legal support is delivered as the company scales.
As Stegra continues to grow, the role offers significant exposure to a broad range of legal and finance matters, close collaboration with internal and external senior stakeholders and executive leadership, and the opportunity to mentor more junior members of the legal team on project finance matters.
Key Responsibilities
As a fast-growing company with cross-over functions between teams, the scope of this role will evolve, however, core responsibilities include:
· Legal Strategy for Debt Financing: Developing, implementing, and maintaining the legal strategy for the company's project and corporate debt financing, in close collaboration with the finance and executive leadership teams.
· Document Negotiation & Drafting: Leading the drafting, negotiation, and execution of legal documentation related to debt financing, including loan agreements, intercreditor agreements, security documents, engagement letters, and other financing-related contracts.
· Stakeholder Coordination: Acting as a primary legal point of contact for debt financing activities, coordinating with internal stakeholders (finance, tax, project delivery, treasury) and external parties (lenders, law firms, consultants, and regulatory bodies).
· Compliance Oversight: Ensuring ongoing compliance with debt-related legal obligations, covenants, and regulatory requirements, and coordinating internal processes to monitor compliance and reporting duties under financing agreements.
· Risk Management: Identifying and mitigating legal risks related to financing structures, securities, and credit support instruments, and providing legal guidance to support informed, risk-based decision-making.
Additional Responsibilities:
· Overseeing covenant compliance processes across multiple lending tranches.
· Coordinating the direct agreement workstream with project counterparties, including EPC, O&M and offtake counterparties, and supporting intercreditor arrangements and multi-party lender coordination.
· Liaising efficiently with lenders' counsel, ECA counsel, technical advisers, insurance advisers, and other external specialists under tight drawdown deadlines.
· Building and maintaining strong relationships with internal stakeholders (finance, tax, treasury, project delivery) and external parties (lenders, investors, law firms, ECAs, and regulatory bodies) on financing-related matters.
· Preparing summaries and reports on financing status, risks, and compliance for internal stakeholders and management.
· Assisting in the preparation of board materials and approvals related to debt financing.
· Supporting the Head of Legal in developing scalable legal processes, templates, and playbooks for the company's project debt financing operations as it grows.
· Providing guidance and oversight to more junior legal team members working on project finance matters, as needed.
Minimum Qualifications
· We are looking for candidates who meet the following criteria:
· A Master of Laws (LL.M. or equivalent) with strong academic credentials.
· Minimum 8 years of relevant legal experience at a leading law firm, within project finance, banking and finance, or capital markets. Relevant in-house experience is also a merit.
· Demonstrated ability to independently lead complex transactional workstreams, from term sheet to complete documentation through drafting, negotiation, and execution, with minimal supervision.
· Strong analytical and drafting skills, with a commercial mindset and sound judgment on risk-based decision-making.
· Effective communication and stakeholder management skills across both legal and finance functions, including engagement with senior leadership.
· Demonstrated ability to manage and organize high-volume transactional document sets, maintain accurate tracking of open items and workstream status, and coordinate effectively across multiple external advisers simultaneously, particularly under deadline-driven transaction timelines.
· A collaborative team player, comfortable working across related financing disciplines and supporting the development of more junior colleagues.
· Fluency in English (written and spoken); additional languages are a plus.
What Will Set You Apart
· Substantial experience in project finance, structured finance, or capital-intensive projects.
· Familiarity with export credit agency (ECA) or public funding financing structures.
· Familiarity with project finance security structures, including pledges, assignments of contract rights, and direct agreements, and with intercreditor or coordination agreement mechanics in multi-tranche lending structures.
· Experience negotiating directly with lenders, ECAs, and their counsel on complex, multi-party financings.
· Experience in corporate or equity financing transactions and M&A, providing broader context across the company's financing activities.
· Experience with company secretarial or corporate governance matters.
· Prior experience mentoring or supervising junior legal team members.
Personal Qualities
We value people who take initiative, build trust, and contribute to a collaborative workplace. You are curious, open to challenging established approaches, and treat others with respect. You are proactive, adaptable, results-driven, and able to prioritize and work independently with full ownership of your responsibilities, while also being ready to guide and support more junior colleagues.
As a person you are likely independent, resilient, proactive and organized. You like to solve complex problems, work in a highly complex environment and have the ability to thrive in a fast-paced and evolving business environment.
Our Stockholm Office
Our modern Stockholm office is located on Norra Stationsgatan, close to Karolinska University Hospital in central Stockholm. Here, you’ll find a bright, collaborative workspace where cross-functional teams connect, share ideas, and drive progress. Whether you're visiting regularly or working hybrid, you'll be part of a vibrant office culture with easy access to the city’s energy and amenities.

jobs.occupation: Mechanical Engineer  From CAD Clean-up to Next-Generation Boat Design
jobs.description: Mechanical Engineer“Make X Shore’s CAD data something production can build from without guessing. Audit and rebuild assemblies, align them with the factory floor, and then help design the next-generation boat.”About the RoleX Shore’s existing CAD models and assemblies don’t fully reflect what’s actually being built on the factory floor — data has drifted from production reality, making it hard to trust drawings, plan rework, or hand off clean information to manufacturing. We’re looking for a Mechanical Engineer to audit and rebuild that CAD data, get it aligned with how boats are actually produced, and then move on to design work on X Shore’s next-generation boat platform.This is a hands-on role in two phases. First, you’ll dig into existing CAD, correct what’s out of sync with production, and work closely with the shop floor to close the gap between design intent and built reality. Once that foundation is solid, you’ll shift into forward-looking platform design for future boats. You’ll report to the Mechanical Engineering & Analysis Manager and be based on-site in Nyköping.Key Responsibilities    Audit existing CAD models and assemblies for accuracy, completeness, and structure    Rebuild or correct CAD data that no longer reflects what’s actually being built in production    Align CAD assemblies and drawings with current production reality, working directly with the shop floor    Identify and resolve discrepancies between design intent and manufactured parts    Maintain clean, well-structured CAD/PDM practices going forward    Support production with drawings, tolerances, and design clarifications during rework and manufacturing    Once alignment work is complete, contribute to the design and detailing of X Shore’s next-generation boat platform    Collaborate with electrical, production, and manufacturing engineering teams to ensure designs are manufacturableRequired Qualifications    Degree in Mechanical Engineering or equivalent practical experience    3-5+ years of experience in mechanical design, ideally in a manufacturing environment    Expert-level SOLIDWORKS proficiency — this is a must-have, including assemblies, drawings, and PDM    Demonstrated experience auditing, cleaning up, or rebuilding CAD data and assemblies    Comfortable working directly with production to resolve build discrepancies    Fluent in English; Swedish is a plus    Ability to work on-site in NyköpingDesirable Qualifications    Experience with composites and/or metals typical of marine or automotive manufacturing    Background in boat building, automotive, or another complex hardware environment    Familiarity with GD&T and tolerance stack-up analysis    Experience contributing to a new product platform from early concept through releasePersonal QualitiesDetail-oriented and methodical, comfortable untangling messy legacy data without losing momentum. Equally at home on the shop floor verifying fit as at a CAD workstation. Takes ownership, follows through, and communicates clearly across engineering and production.Success Metrics (First 12 Months)    CAD data and assemblies for existing boats are audited, corrected, and aligned with what’s built in production    Production has accurate, trustworthy drawings and models to work from    Discrepancies between design and manufactured parts are identified and resolved    Meaningful contribution made to next-generation boat platform designLocation & StructureOn-site at X Shore Factory & HQ, Nyköping. Reports to the Mechanical Engineering & Analysis Manager.

Mat4Green Tech AB (M4GT) is a Chalmers University spin-out based in Gothenburg. We develop and commercialise closed-loop processes for recovering and refining metals from industrial materials, with our own lab and pilot facilities in Gothenburg. We are now looking for a chemist who will take hands-on ownership of our recycling and purification work.About the roleYou will run and develop hydrometallurgical and electrochemical processes in our lab and pilot facility, from leaching and solvent extraction to electrolysis and final purification. You plan, build and manage your own projects: you define what equipment and materials are needed, find and negotiate with suppliers, carry purchases through, and keep the work documented and safe. You work closely with our technical team and take the process forward step by step towards industrial scale.What we are looking for    A Master's degree or higher in chemistry, chemical engineering or a related field    - A solid understanding of process chemistry, including solvent extraction and electrolysis, and of safe handling of the chemicals involved    - Experience in planning, writing up and managing technical projects    - A structured and efficient way of working, with the ability to adapt when conditions change    - The ability to find, negotiate and purchase the equipment and materials needed to carry out the job    - Fluent English; Swedish is a meritWhat we offerA key role in a technically strong team with close ties to Chalmers, a high degree of ownership, and the opportunity to take a process from the lab to industrial scale.ApplicationSend your CV and a short cover letter by e-mail. Interviews are held on a rolling basis, so apply as soon as possible.

The Plant Coordinator supports the coordination and management of plant, vehicles, tools, and assets across operations in Sweden. The role supports asset management activities, lifecycle planning, and operational asset performance. The role supports plant availability, maintenance coordination, and efficient utilisation of company assets. The role works with internal stakeholders, suppliers, and service providers to support asset management, regulatory compliance, and commercial objectives.How this role lives our values This role supports the effective management of plant and assets by helping ensure that equipment, vehicles, and resources are available, maintained, and correctly managed throughout their lifecycle. By maintaining visibility of asset performance, availability, and compliance requirements, the role supports efficient operations and informed decision-making. Safety: Support a safe working environment by helping ensure assets, vehicles, equipment, and inspection requirements are managed in accordance with company and regulatory standards. Integrity: Support accuracy, accountability, and compliance through effective record management, asset tracking, and adherence to established processes. Teamwork: Build strong working relationships that support collaboration, communication, and coordinated asset management activities. Ownership: Take responsibility for following through on actions, resolving operational issues, and supporting the effective management of company assets. Sustainability: Support long-term value creation through responsible asset management, efficient utilisation, and sustainable lifecycle practices. Key ResponsibilitiesPlant & Asset Lifecycle Management:     Coordinate plant, vehicle, tool, and asset activities throughout the asset lifecycle, including receipt, return, allocation, and disposal in line with project requirements.     Support asset management strategies and asset replacement or upgrade planning. Maintenance & Compliance Coordination:     Coordinate planned and unplanned maintenance activities, inspections, testing requirements, and equipment compliance activities.     Maintain up-to-date asset records, tracking information, and compliance documentation, including leased and hired assets. Asset Operations & Procurement Support:     Coordinate plant movements, operational requirements, procurement activities, and supplier engagement.     Support commercial decision-making relating to plant acquisition, hire, utilisation, and cost management.     Support the procurement of fuel, spare parts, and other plant-related requirements. Sustainability & Asset Optimisation:     Support effective asset utilisation, reuse, sale, recycling, and sustainability initiatives in line with the company’s sustainability strategy. Fleet & Incident Coordination:     Coordinate fleet-related incidents, repairs, and recovery activities.    Coordinate vehicle maintenance requirements in line with applicable regional requirements. Health, Safety & Regulatory Compliance:     Support compliance with safety, environmental, sustainability, regulatory, and internal company requirements. Commercial Administration:     Support the effective management of plant and asset-related costs.     Reconcile monthly invoices and account statements relating to plant and assets. Key Requirements     3rd level qualification or equivalent experience in procurement, purchasing, commercial functions, or construction plant operations.     Experience in a similar position (typically 3 years or more).     Knowledge of plant and asset management.     Knowledge of Swedish regulatory requirements and construction industry standards.     Experience using asset management systems and tools.     Analytical skills, process awareness, and attention to detail.     Communication, relationship management, and stakeholder engagement skills.     Fluent English; Swedish language skills are advantageous.     Valid Swedish or EEA driver's licence.Skills     Plant and asset management knowledge.     Regulatory compliance knowledge.     Asset management systems knowledge.     Analytical and process management skills.     Stakeholder engagement and relationship management skills.     Commercial awareness. TECHLA is a Gothenburg-based consulting company working with modern product development across software, embedded systems, cloud and DevOps.We started TECHLA with a simple idea: to build the kind of consulting company we would want to work for ourselves. We want to build long-term relationships, work with great people and create an environment where both our consultants and our clients can thrive.We believe in transparency, trust and giving people the freedom and responsibility to grow. Our consultants should feel that they are part of something, have a real influence and are rewarded for the value they create.At TECHLA, technology matters – but people matter even more. We believe the best results come from skilled people who take ownership, work closely together and genuinely care about what they deliver.We are big enough to deliver, but small enough to care.Would you like to build digital products and services that connect vehicles, customers and the people who keep vehicles on the road?TECHLA is looking for experienced full-stack developers for assignments in automotive and connected services. You’ll work in product teams developing everything from customer-facing applications to cloud-based services and integrations.The technology stack varies by assignment. It may include React and TypeScript on the frontend, with backend services built using Java and Spring Boot, C#/.NET, Node.js, Python or Go. Teams work with cloud platforms such as AWS and Azure.What you’ll work onDepending on the assignment, you may:    Design, build and maintain frontend applications using React and TypeScript    Develop backend services, APIs and integrations    Connect user-facing applications to cloud services and distributed systems    Work with microservices and event-driven architectures    Build and operate solutions on AWS or Azure    Develop automated tests and improve CI/CD, monitoring and service reliability    Contribute to technical design, code reviews and architecture discussions    Take features from requirements and design through implementation, testing and productionWhat we’re looking for    Several years of professional full-stack development experience, typically five or more    Hands-on experience developing both frontend and backend functionality    Strong frontend skills in React and TypeScript, or comparable modern web technologies    Strong backend experience in at least one relevant stack, such as Java/Spring Boot, C#/.NET, Node.js, Python or Go    Experience building APIs, integrations or distributed applications    Experience with AWS and/or Azure    A good understanding of testing, code quality and maintainable software    The ability to collaborate with colleagues across product, design and engineering    Fluent English; Swedish is a plus.    A degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering or a related field.It’s a plus if you have    GraphQL, Kafka or other event-streaming technologies    AWS serverless services such as Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB or SQS    Kubernetes, Docker and CI/CD    SQL and NoSQL databases    Experience from automotive, connected vehicles, telecom or other product-focused environments    Experience operating and improving production servicesThe mindset we’re looking forFor us, being a great engineer is about more than technical skills.We’re looking for people with a strong consulting mindset – people who understand that great consulting is about creating real value, taking ownership and being someone both the team and the client can rely on.You’re highly skilled at what you do, but you’re also a doer who cares about quality. You don’t wait for someone else to solve the problem. You take initiative, move things forward and care about delivering work you can genuinely be proud of.At the same time, you genuinely enjoy working with others. You communicate openly, share knowledge, contribute to a positive team dynamic and believe that the best results are created together.You take responsibility for the bigger picture, stay solution-oriented and aren’t afraid to go the extra mile when it makes a difference. At the same time, you’re humble, genuine and enjoy working with people who challenge and support each other.In short, we’re looking for engineers who want to go beyond – technically, professionally and as part of a team.We’re open to both employment and freelance/subcontractor setups – so whether you’re looking to join TECHLA or take on your next assignment as an independent consultant, we’d love to hear from you.Feel free to reach out to johanna.bornemyr@techla.se or submit your application, and we’ll be happy to tell you more about the opportunities.

It helps us build a pipeline so we can act quickly when we receive a new assignment.When we get a relevant request from a client, we will review applications from this ad and contact candidates whose profile matches the specific requirements. This also means you may not hear from us in between, as there may be no active assignment at the time.Demand for this role can change quickly, and during the summer period it may not always be active.Temp-Team Sweden AB is supporting one of the world’s leading and most recognized tech companies in recruiting Logistics/Warehouse Support staff for their Data Center in Gävle. If you are looking for a dynamic role in a high-performing environment, with opportunities to develop your skills within logistics, inventory management, and warehouse operations, this could be the right opportunity for you.You will play a vital part in making the Data Centers daily operations run smoothly. If this sounds interesting, send a targeted CV (in English) and we will review it and get back to you if there's a match.It is very important that you communicate your experience within the above mentioned job details and requirements in your CV.For any questions regarding the position please contact Elnaz Memarian at elm@temp-team.se

Research shows that women and other under-represented groups within our industry hesitate to apply unless they tick most boxes of a role description. At Stegra, we are building an impact company with sustainability at its core. We need a diverse, inclusive, and authentic team to rally behind our purpose of de-carbonizing hard-to-abate industries, starting with steel.So, if you are equally passionate about our purpose yet concerned that your experience doesn’t perfectly align with the qualifications stated in the job advert, we strongly encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate, either for this role – or for another upcoming role in our rapidly growing business.About us:Stegra is on a mission to disrupt the global steel industry by producing green steel, with the end goal of bringing down CO2 emissions to zero. By using green hydrogen and fossil-free electricity instead of coal; water and heat will be our primary emissions. By 2030, our ambition is to produce 5 million tonnes of green steel annually in our fully integrated, digitalized, and sustainable plant in Boden, located in northern Sweden - currently in construction phase. But this is just the beginning – our expertise in green hydrogen will enable us to decarbonize other industries in addition to steel, and we look forward to what’s next in store for us.We are looking for talented, innovative, and purpose-driven people to join our rapidly growing and diverse team. Our employees get to learn everyday, implement the latest technology and test and put their ideas into practice. Together, we are building an impact company with sustainability at its core – for our people, customers, investors, society, and planet.Work location: BodenWhat you’ll doRight now, we are looking for a Project Engineer for our Project Delivery team. In this role you will work closely with our Groundworks Manager, Construction teams, EPCM Area Leads, planners, and contractors to support the delivery of civil and early works across the Boden project.As Project Engineer, you will help turn engineering packages into construction-ready scopes. You will coordinate documentation, interfaces, and execution requirements to ensure workfronts are properly prepared before being released to contractors. This is a hands-on role suited to someone who enjoys working close to both engineering and site execution.Specific to this role, the day-to-day tasks will include the following but as we are a growing company with very little silos between teams, other tasks might be included as well.    Coordinate preparation and release of groundworks scopes, ensuring drawings, quantities, and execution requirements are ready for construction    Maintain the Groundworks Scope Tracker and consolidate inputs from EPCM partners, design teams, and planners    Support forecasting and planning of upcoming groundworks activities    Coordinate scope clarifications between Engineering, Planning, Construction, and contractors    Support and maintain a structured RFI process between contractors and engineering stakeholders    Help align groundworks activities with project schedules, civil milestones, and interface dependencies    Participate in coordination meetings and support progress reporting and issue resolution    Monitor contractor readiness, access conditions, and documentation prior to site executionWhat you’ll bringYou’re curious and believe that real progress happens when we work together. You’re not afraid to challenge old ways of thinking and you treat others with respect while doing it. At Stegra, we value people who take initiative, build trust, and help create a workplace where everyone can do their best.This role is well suited to someone who has built a solid foundation in civil engineering or construction and wants to continue developing in a large-scale industrial project environment.Specific to this role, we would like to see that you can tick off a fair amount of the boxes below    Degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, or a related technical field    Around 3–7 years of experience from large-scale industrial, construction, or infrastructure projects    Good understanding of civil construction, design documentation, and site execution    Experience working in EPCM, contractor, or major project environments is considered an advantage    Strong coordination skills and the ability to work across multiple teams and disciplines    Familiarity with Primavera P6 or similar planning tools is considered an advantage    Experience with Swedish AMA/AB04 standards is considered a plus    Fluency in English; Swedish is considered an advantage

As Head of the Avionics & Electrical Department, you will play a central role in shaping the electrical and electronic architecture of our satellite platforms and ensuring the reliable performance of our missions. Our customers include major space companies, agencies, and commercial players across Europe and worldwide.OHB Sweden develops advanced small satellite systems for scientific and Earth observation missions. These missions require highly reliable avionics and electrical systems that form the backbone of the spacecraft, enabling power generation and distribution, communications, command and data handling, and mission operations.The Avionics & Electrical Department is responsible for the design, development, verification, and support of the satellite's electrical and electronic systems. The department currently consists of approximately 23 highly skilled engineers and specialists working in areas including:    Electrical Architecture    Electrical Power Systems (EPS)    TT&C and Communications Systems and RF Systems    EMC / EMI    Electronics Design    Radiation Engineering and EEE Component Usage    Data Handling Systems and Onboard Computers    Harness Design    FPGA Design    EGSE designThe department contributes throughout the complete spacecraft lifecycle, from early mission concepts and proposal activities, through design studies, detailed development, subsystem and system verification, launch preparation, and operational support.The space industry is evolving rapidly, driven by increased satellite autonomy, software-defined systems, miniaturized electronics, higher levels of integration, growing constellation markets, and increasing demands on cybersecurity, resilience, and manufacturability. At the same time, OHB Sweden is transitioning towards a higher degree of productization and industrialization of its satellite platforms. In this context, the Avionics & Electrical Department will play a key role in defining future platform architectures, technologies, methodologies, and engineering practices. As Head of Department, you will lead this evolution and ensure OHB Sweden remains a competitive and technically leading provider of advanced small satellite systems.As Head of the Avionics & Electrical Department, you will be mainly responsible for:    Driving staff recruitment, onboarding, and development to build a motivated and high-performing team.    Managing resource planning to balance project demands and support business growth, in close collaboration with project managers and other department heads.    Acting as a key point of contact for customers, partners, and suppliers on avionics, electrical, communications, electronics, and onboard computing matters.    Ensures that engineering processes relevant for the department activities exist and are properly implemented.    Ensures that proper engineering tools are efficiently used in the department    Owns the department ways-of-working.    Implementing strategic and operational decisions from the Company Management Team within the department.    Ensuring the department's skills and expertise align with the evolving needs of the company and its projects.    Reporting to employees and managers.    Overall responsibility for the technical deliveries from the department to the project in quality, time and cost.    Managing resource planning to balance project demands and support business growth, in close collaboration with project managers and other department heads.    Contributing to proposals by estimating costs and evaluating staffing.    Leading budgeting within your area of responsibility, covering general expenses, training, laboratories, equipment, and investments.What We're Looking For    Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Engineering Physics, or a related discipline.    At least 10 years of experience as an engineer and technical leader within avionics, electronics, electrical systems, communications, or a related field.    Proven leadership skills, with experience managing teams and coordinating complex, multidisciplinary engineering activities.    Strong understanding of spacecraft avionics and electrical systems, including electrical architectures, power systems, communications, onboard computing, electronics development and testing.    Understanding of EMC, radiation effects, reliability, and engineering standards applicable to space systems.    Strong analytical skills and the ability to foster innovation and continuous improvement within the team.    Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.    Fluency in English; knowledge of Swedish is a plus. jobs.description: Job DescriptionThe Engineering Manager (EM) is accountable for technical execution, delivery quality, and operational excellence for a defined product or service. The role partners with Product Managers in product contexts and owns delivery and roadmap in service contexts. The EM combines delivery accountability with people leadership and has the mandate to make technical decisions aligned with strategy.    ABOUT THE TEAM The Pricing Foundation Team is a global product development team at H&M Group, driving the future of pricing across our brands and markets. We bring together product, business, engineering, quality assurance, analytics, and design expertise to build scalable solutions that enable accurate, automated, and data-driven pricing decisions. Working across Stockholm and Bangalore, we collaborate closely as one team to deliver business-critical capabilities that impact millions of customers worldwide.  ABOUT THE SCOPE Our team owns the core pricing platform that powers H&M Group's global pricing operations. We are responsible for developing and evolving services that ensure consistent, scalable, and reliable pricing across brands, channels, and markets. By combining modern technology, automation, and strong business collaboration, we enable faster time to market, improved data quality, and seamless pricing experiences while supporting H&M's digital transformation journey. We're on an ambitious transformation journey, redefining how pricing works across H&M Group. For our team members, this means the opportunity to work with modern technologies, solve complex business challenges at scale, and grow alongside a product area that is shaping the future of global retail pricing.  WHO YOU ARE      Deep expertise in engineering (end-to-end development process understanding)       Deep expertise in architecture, scalable design principles and cloud fundamentals      Familiarity with automated build, test, and deployment pipelines – CI/CD & DevOps     Ability to assess and manage technical debt.       Hands-on capability to stay up to date with the technology being led       Coaching and leadership skills.       Strong communication and stakeholder management.       Experience in vendor collaboration and external partnerships.       Financial acumen – ability to manage tech budgets.       Strong understanding of agile ways of working, including continuous improvement practices.       Ability to balance technical trade-offs with business priorities.       Analytical thinking: leveraging data and insights to inform decisions.       Ability to navigate complexity and ambiguity.       Strong security & compliance skills, securing coding and regulatory awareness       Understanding of monitoring, incident management and SRE practices     And who has..      Strong in engineering and architecture expertise      Ability to manage technical debt      Strong stakeholder communication skills      Vendor collaboration experience      Financial/budget awareness      Strong agile ways of working      Security and compliance understanding      Monitoring and incident management knowledge  WHO WE ARE  H&M Group is a global company of strong fashion brands and ventures. Our goal is to prove that there is no compromise between exceptional design, affordable prices, and sustainable solutions. We want to liberate fashion for the many, and our customers are at the heart of every decision we make.  We are made up of thousands of passionate and talented colleagues united by our shared culture and values. Together, we want to use our power, our scale, and our knowledge to push the fashion industry towards a more inclusive and sustainable future.   WHY YOU’LL LOVE WORKING HERE  At H&M Group, we are proud to be a vibrant and welcoming company. We offer our employees attractive benefits with extensive development opportunities around the globe.      Staff discount card: Usable on all our H&M Group brands in stores and online.      H&M Incentive Program (HIP): Included in our HIP. You can read more about our H&M Incentive Program here.      Competitive pensions: Collective Agreement and ITP pensions competitive to the Swedish market.      Generous vacation: 30 days' vacation, health care allowance, and good work-life balance.      Additional perks: Discounts from Benify.      Innovative Environment: Work with cutting-edge technology and innovative solutions.      Global Impact: Be part of a team that influences users worldwide.      Professional Growth: Endless opportunities to learn and develop your skills.      Collaborative Culture: Join a motivated team that values collaboration and excellence.   JOIN US  Our uniqueness comes from a combination of many things – our inclusive and collaborative culture, our strong values, and opportunities for growth. But most of all, it’s our people who make us who we are.  This is a full-time permanent position, starting as soon as possible according to the agreement. The role is a hybrid position, based in our office in Stockholm, Sweden.  Apply by sending in your CV in English as soon as possible. Due to data policies, we only accept applications through the career page.  Take the next step in your career together with us. The journey starts here. We are eager to meet you!  *We are committed to a recruitment process that is fair, equitable, and based on competency. We therefore kindly ask you to not attach a cover letter in your application. RaySearch develops innovative software solutions to improve cancer care. Over 1200 clinics in more than 54 countries use RaySearch software to improve treatments and quality of life for patients. RaySearch was founded in 2000 and is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm. The headquarters is located in Stockholm, with subsidiaries in the US, Europe, Asia and Australia & New Zealand. Today we are more than 485 employees with a common vision of improving cancer care with innovative software. Our great staff is crucial for our success and we offer a fantastic working environment in modern offices, flexibility and good opportunities for development. We believe in equal opportunities, value diversity and work actively to prevent discrimination.Do you have experience in software test management and want to improve cancer care for patients around the world? Join RaySearch's development department as Verification and Validation Manager for RayCare! About the position RayCare is an innovative oncology information system designed to support clinical workflows at cancer clinics. It is developed by multiple agile teams working closely together, with expertise spanning clinical workflows, integrations, and system architecture. We develop our products in close collaboration with leading cancer clinics worldwide. As Verification and Validation Manager for RayCare, you will be part of the RaySearch Product Safety team and play a central role in ensuring product quality throughout the development lifecycle. Together with the team, you will plan, lead, and document development projects, ensuring that we deliver safe and high-quality software to our users. In this role, you will work closely with development teams, product management, and other stakeholders across the organization. The work is dynamic and cross-functional, requiring both structure and adaptability. Your main tasks     Develop, own, and continuously evolve the Verification and Validation strategy for RayCare releases.    Lead the associated V&V activities in accordance with RaySearch development and risk management processes, using a risk-based and lifecycle-oriented approach that supports product quality and regulatory compliance.     Ensure fit-for-purpose test environments, test tools, and ways of working that enable teams to implement the Verification and Validation strategy effectively.      Drive continuous improvement of V&V execution, with a particular focus on increased automation.     Create compliant V&V documentation, including test specifications, reports, and V&V summaries. Your profile We believe that you have a background as a verification and validation manager or a similar leading role within software testing. You are pragmatic in your approach and able to structure and prioritize work in a dynamic environment. You enjoy solving problems as they arise and take initiative to improve ways of working— - especially when it comes to automation and efficiency. You are comfortable coordinating across with teams and stakeholders and have strong communication skills. Requirements     BSc or MSc degree in engineering, or equivalent     5+ years of experience in verification and validation management within software development     Excellent written and spoken communication skills (English and Swedish) Meriting     Strong experience driving test automation and working with system integrations in complex environments    Experience coordinating validation usability testing and working within agile development methodologies    Background in the MedTech industry, with hands-on experience applying AI-driven and agentic testing approaches Our CultureCulture at RaySeach is the driving force behind our organization, where everything we do is driven by a shared passion for innovation and the fight against cancer. Our dedication is reflected in our ability to deliver exceptional results, pay close attention to detail, and consistently go the extra mile. Our employees stand out as experts in their field, driven by a relentless focus on solving problems - no matter how complex. At RaySearch, we take pride in leading the way in cancer treatment, leveraging cutting-edge technology to develop innovative solutions that make a real difference in patient care.Our OfferAt RaySearch, we offer a diverse and inclusive work environment, fostering openness, sincerity, and collaboration. Located in Hagastaden, Stockholm's Life Science Hub, our modern and creative workspace includes an in-house gym, yoga, and social activities like ping pong, table football, and regular after-work events. Our bistro serves a fantastic lunch buffet, and we offer morning- and afternoon-fika every day. Our rooftop terrace also provides a stunning 360-degree view of Stockholm, enhancing the work experience. All of this comes attached with a competitive compensation and benefits package.ApplicationPlease apply to the position through the application form below. We do not accept applications by e-mail. Selection and interviews will be ongoing.

Silex Microsystems is the world’s leading pure-play MEMS foundry, customizing solutions for prominent global clients in industries such as pharmaceuticals, consumer electronics, and automotive. As a Process Engineer, you will initiate and drive progress in the Plasma Deposition area. Sounds interesting? Keep reading.Would you like to know more about Silex and what we do?The AreaThe Plasma deposition area is one of several vital departments of our production line here at Silex. Several different deposition techniques (PVD, PECVD, ALD and evaporation) are utilized to deposit thin films, ranging from various metals to dielectrics.You will work with both engineers, process operators and service technicians where collaboration is critical to ensure good process stability, tool uptime and continuous improvement.The roleYour overall responsibility is to ensure manufacturing goals are met, together with operators and service technicians. Your days will be a mix of meetings with Product Managers, developing new processes that meet customers' specifications and ensure reliable production processes.You will also participate in creating work routines for operators and solve problems that occur at the area, driving improvement projects to enhance our workflow and processes at the Plasma Deposition area.In this role, you will:    Develop, maintain and improve thin film deposition processes.    Establish, and maintain routines and documentation.    Handle stopped production batches and development material together with process integration engineers (PIs).    Be a part of creating and improving the infrastructure for operator training to make sure current routine is available and up to date.    Participate in process qualification of new equipment or materials and release them to production.    Participate in the startup of new products, review specifications and process flows.    Grow into taking responsibility for area equipment, improving the tool uptime, maintain and develop new standardized process modules.We are looking for someone who has:    A PhD degree in relevant field, or a Master’s degree combined with a couple of years of relevant industrial experience. Specializing in Nanotechnology, Microfabrication, Applied Physics or Material Science is considered as highly beneficial.    An understanding of plasma physics or semiconductor processing principles. Hands-on experience with deposition equipment, e.g. PVD, PECVD, ALD and evaporation is considered a merit.    The ability to see opportunities for improvement and manage projects to follow through with those improvements.    Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work effectively in a team environment.    Strong skills in documentation and quality management    Excellent communication skills in English; proficiency in Swedish is considered a merit.What we offer you    An opportunity to work closely with talented and inspiring colleagues in a collaborative environment.    A chance to be part of a world-leading company, driving the future of MEMS technology.    The ability to engage with cutting-edge innovations that shape global industries and everyday life.    The satisfaction of contributing directly to transformative technologies at the industry’s most advanced pure-play MEMS foundry.About Silex Silex is the world’s largest and most advanced pure-play MEMS foundry, headquartered in Stockholm. MEMS technology is moving into an abundance of modern innovations; from data centers, consumer and automotive electronics to medical diagnostics and life science.The recruitment process We have an ongoing recruitment process, so we encourage you to submit your application as soon as possible. To apply, please attach your CV and answer a few brief questions. Our process is competency-based and includes a personality and logic test, reference checks, and a background check. Additionally, a drug test will be conducted prior to employment, and we perform random alcohol and drug tests for all employees.

At Embark, we are exploring what it means to build living games by choosing the smartest route while striving towards a healthy work-life balance. As a Senior Producer on ARC Raiders, you will join the game’s core leadership team, working in close partnership with the Executive Producer, production leads, and discipline leads to safeguard the quality, player sentiment, and ongoing product direction of our live game.We see game development, especially in a live environment, as a constant work in progress and a living journey. In this role, you will be a product-minded leader with a strong appetite for community engagement and external communication. While our Production Director owns studio planning, P&L, and staffing, you will focus on the "What" and "Why" and the player impact. In close collaboration with the directors, you will help assess what is best for our players, deeply understanding why we make specific choices. You will focus on product health, drive update quality, and ensure that player feedback directly informs our live strategy. You will manage expectations upward, delegate with trust, and champion creative ideas that don't just meet expectations, but actively surprise and delight our community.Examples of Responsibilities    Product Ownership & Alignment: Sit on the ARC Raiders leadership team, collaborating with the EP, production leads, and discipline leads to drive product strategy and translate vision into high-quality live updates.    Game Quality & Sentiment Ownership: Serve as the guardian for update quality, player sentiment, and product health to ensure every release, feature, and patch lands with high polish and positive player response.    Community Connection & External Communication: Partner closely with the Community Team to listen to player feedback, translate insights into actionable game updates, and help shape clear, empathetic communication directly with our community.    Living Product Mindset: Embrace the reality that a live game is under constant evolution, guiding the game's direction through iteration, community sentiment, and data-informed decision-making.    Expectation Management & Delegation: Manage product expectations upward to executive stakeholders and internally across the studio, knowing when to step in, when to delegate, and how to empower cross-functional teams.    Collaborative Problem-Solving & Delight: Work shoulder-to-shoulder with cross-functional feature teams to solve complex creative and product challenges while fostering an environment where teams are empowered to take creative risks that delight players.We would love if you have    8+ years of experience in AAA PC or console games production, including experience as a Product Owner, Senior Lead Producer, or Game Lead on a major live-service (GaaS) title.    Proven track record of owning product strategy and live quality, with a strong emphasis on player retention, community sentiment, and post-launch engagement.    Deep curiosity and understanding of game design, player motivations, understanding feedback and data, product rationale, and being able to grasp and articulate why specific choices are made for the game and community.    A strong appetite for external communication and community dynamics and are comfortable acting as a bridge between internal game development and the player base.    A mindset that views games as living software and are comfortable navigating constant change and viewing live game development as an ongoing journey.    Strong leadership presence & capability to build high-trust partnerships with production and discipline leads.    Exceptional communication skills with a focus on collaboration, empathetic player engagement, and strong collaboration & delegation habits.    Deep passion for PC/console games, competitive/co-op multiplayer ecosystems, and community dynamics. This is an on-site role, and we are only considering candidates already residing in Sweden.At Embark we offer competitive salaries, passionate colleagues to share knowledge with and much more, but most of all we invite you to take part of a journey into the unknown, to build creative, surprising and beautiful experiences together.Be yourself at Embark and make games while doing so. Please apply with confidence. We can’t wait to hear from you (in English)!

Part-time freelance | Small Groups

Do people describe you as a storyteller? Are you the friend who always ends up explaining the history, recommending the hidden café, or connecting the dots? Do you love Stockholm — not just the postcard version, but the layers beneath it?

Then keep reading.

Amitylux is a multi-award-winning boutique travel company creating high-touch, personal guided experiences across the Nordics and the UK. We focus on small groups, meaningful conversations, and experiences that feel natural rather than scripted. Our tours are relaxed, human, and built around connection. We value calm, confident leadership. We value thoughtful storytelling that adapts to the group. We value presence, awareness, and reading the room. Our guests come from all over the world — from curious leisure travellers to corporate and VIP groups. What they all appreciate is authenticity, quality, and a genuine sense of welcome rather than being processed.

You Might Be a Great Fit If You:

• 
Can turn strangers into friends within a few hours

• 
Feel comfortable leading while staying warm and approachable

• 
Have lived in Stockholm long enough to truly understand it

• 
Plan to stay and grow here

• 
Speak fluent English (additional languages are a strong plus)

• 
Enjoy walking and being outdoors

• 
Understand that guiding is both performance and hospitality

This is not about memorising dates. It’s about creating a feeling people remember.

What You’ll Experience With Us

• 
A supportive, high-standard team culture

• 
Autonomy and trust

• 
The chance to meet people from around the world

• 
The opportunity to grow your leadership and storytelling skills

• 
Being part of a brand that cares deeply about guest experience

We take pride in what we do — and we look for people who feel the same.

Join us on this journey — and help shape meaningful travel experiences in Stockholm.
